We are looking for a Senior Coastal Engineer to join our growing global coastal team. This position could be located in Vancouver or Halifax.

Our coastal team primarily serves projects with ports and marine engineering needs and support sectors within the business, e.g., Infrastructure, Mining, Metals, Energy and Environment.  The primary role is to lead coastal engineering project scopes and to provide technical support, guidance, and mentorship in all coastal related project aspects from concept phases to delivery.

Ideally your expertise should cover the following coastal skills:

Defining metocean in-situ data collection campaigns based on project scope requirements. Hands-on field and instrumentation experience is an asset.

Studying, defining and providing coastal engineering related design basis inputs to structural basis of design for the domains of marine and port structural engineering.

Sound knowledge on data processing of vast environmental data sets, including but not limited to, hindcast data, measured data, statistical analysis methods, etc.

Coastal protection design based on hard engineering (breakwater, groins, revetment), and alternative soft engineering solutions (beach nourishment or habitat creation). Experience with physical modelling, design implementation and construction methodologies is an asset.

Dredging: design, methodologies, and material disposal.

Hydrodynamic (waves, tides, and flow) and sediment transport numerical modeling. Tsunami modeling is an asset.

Mooring analysis based on static and dynamic numerical models.

Understanding of the overall port development and planning phases and aspects, including navigation, and weather dependent downtime.

The ideal candidate should possess a relevant degree and be able to demonstrate experience in the skills listed above and below:

B.Sc., B.Eng., M.Sc., or M.Eng. degree in Civil, Coastal or Ocean Engineering and Ocean Science

Professional designation (e.g., engineering, geoscientist or equivalent)

Minimum 12+ years of experience in engineering and design of coastal structures

Performing engineering calculations, and preparing design drawings

Numerical models (e.g., SWAN, Delft3D, DHI Mike models, AQUA, Optimoor)

Knowledge and application of international best practice and relevant local standards and guidelines

Ability to work independently and in a team, depending on the project scope

Provide technical mentorship to graduate and junior level engineers

jobs.description:
Requisition ID:  176124 

Job Level:  Senior Level 

Home District/Group:  Kiewit Infrastructure Engineers 

Department:  Design Engineering 

Market:  Marine 

Employment Type:  Full Time 

Position Overview 

Kiewit is expanding its design team specializing in Marine & Coastal Resiliency (MCR) and is seeking top performing contributors to support and sustain its growth. As such, we are currently looking for a  Senior Marine Structural Engineer  specializing in marine infrastructure projects. This role presents a unique opportunity to act as an internal engineer at Kiewit , with access to Kiewit’s resources and experience to ensure that design work is carried out with the best constructability guidelines in the market. 

The Senior Marine Structural Engineer will work closely with an interdisciplinary team that includes coastal, civil and geotechnical engineers, as well as estimators, schedulers and other construction professionals to provide various services to clients for the development of MCR projects. 

The Senior Marine Structural Engineer will be responsible to lead out preliminary and detailed structural design efforts on marine infrastructure projects, supporting engineering integration, managing design, providing technical mentorship to team members, and contributing to construction estimating, scheduling, and planning efforts. Additionally, they will be responsible for connecting with the Operating Districts, developing a strong trusting relationship with the main stakeholders in districts, understanding their engineering support needs in the Marine, Ports, Maritime, and Coastal space. The successful candidate will contribute with their energy, enthusiasm, collaborative approach, and leadership to achieve the quality and safety objectives of the projects to which they are assigned. 

District Overview 

Kiewit Infrastructure Engineering seamlessly transitions solutions from design to construction through the collaborative efforts of Design Engineering, Design Management, Proposals, Estimating, and Integrated Project Controls. Our construction-focused engineering approach involves a multidisciplinary team working together to maximize value for clients by improving schedules, controlling costs, and minimizing risk on infrastructure projects. This integrated strategy emphasizes collaboration and constructability throughout the project lifecycle, enabling us to identify and implement quality solutions with a strong safety focus.  

Clients benefit from Kiewit’s proven processes and tools, which minimize project risk. As an in-house resource, we support projects across the company, in all major markets, sharing experiences, innovative concepts, and best practices. Kiewit’s management and implementation of this process result in safe, cost-effective, and innovative designs that exceed client expectations and uphold Kiewit’s legacy of excellence.  

At Kiewit, we believe in building more than just structures – we build relationships, strengthen communities, and expand workforce capacity. We don't just build projects; we build careers. With top-notch health benefits, a wealth-building 401k plan, and unbeatable growth opportunities, we are deeply invested in the future of our employees. Join us at Kiewit, where we go beyond construction to develop the ultimate road to success. 

Location 

This position could be based out of the following locations:  

Houston, TX  

Fort Worth, TX 

Raleigh, NC  

Opportunity for relocation asssitance available for qualified candidates, more remote working opportunities would be considered with additional travel to offices/projects.  

Responsibilities 

Act as a Senior Marine Structural Engineer as part of the Marine & Coastal Resiliency design team on pursuits and projects, including: 

Perform, review, and oversee structural analysis and design for marine structures, 

Develop detailed construction drawings and specifications, 

Prepare technical reports and documentation, 

Ensure accuracy of design deliverables (reports, drawings & specifications, etc.), 

Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to ensure project success, 

Conduct site inspections and provide technical support during construction, 

Help identify design risks and assist with risk mitigation planning, 

Unique to the Kiewit model: act as a facilitator of collaboration with construction teams during the design phase. Take advantage of access to the construction team to achieve a design that is truly optimal for construction. 

Perform project coordination and management of selected engineering projects. 

Mentor and lead engineers in their technical development. 

Contribute to MCR technical proposals. 

Support the development of the MCR engineering team by building internal tools and processes. 

Qualifications 

Bachelor’s degree in civil/Structural Engineering or equivalent. A master’s degree is an asset. 

10+ years’ experience in structural engineering of marine structures such as; Piers, floating Docks, sea walls, wharfs and mooring dolphins 

Experienced in performing a berthing & mooring analysis and design of marine fenders. 

Familiar with marine terminals operations 

Experience with project delivery models that include working directly with the contractor is an asset (one or several of Early Contractor Involvement, Design-Build, Progressive Design-Build, etc.). 

Professional Engineer P.E. license required. 

Strong communication, problem-solving and organizational skills. 

Proficient in English, proficiency in Spanish or French is an asset 

Efficiency, autonomy, initiative, and ability to prioritize.

Other Requirements:

Regular, reliable attendance 

Work productively and meet deadlines timely

Communicate and interact effectively and professionally with supervisors, employees, and others individually or in a team environment.

Perform work safely and effectively. Understand and follow oral and written instructions, including warning signs, equipment use, and other policies.

Work during normal operating hours to organize and complete work within given deadlines. Work overtime and weekends as required.

May work at various different locations and conditions may vary.

Our construction-focused engineering approach involves a multidisciplinary team working together to maximize value for clients by improving schedules, controlling costs, and minimizing risk on infrastructure projects. This integrated strategy emphasizes collaboration and constructability throughout the project lifecycle, enabling us to identify and implement quality solutions with a strong safety focus.

Clients benefit from Kiewit’s proven processes and tools, which minimize project risk. As an in-house resource, we support projects across the company, in all major markets, sharing experiences, innovative concepts, and best practices. Kiewit’s management and implementation of this process result in safe, cost-effective, and innovative designs that exceed client expectations and uphold Kiewit’s legacy of excellence.

At Kiewit, we believe in building more than just structures – we build relationships, strengthen communities, and expand workforce capacity. We don't just build projects; we build careers. With top-notch health benefits, a wealth-building 401k plan (RRSP), and unbeatable growth opportunities, we are deeply invested in the future of our employees. Join us at Kiewit, where we go beyond construction to develop the ultimate road to success.

Location 

This position is based out of our Lone Tree, Colorado office and includes travel to project offices as needed. One of the many things that makes Kiewit’s culture unique is that we go where the work is, which exposes your career to abundant opportunities. We prioritize work-life balance by offering a flexible work schedule.

Responsibilities 

· Working on preliminary engineering designs and EPC/design-build pursuits and projects; developing design recommendations and producing design deliverables; serving as lead structural engineer and engineer of record with responsibility for design recommendations and deliverables.

· Ensuring designs are completed with consistent application of design standards, technical approaches, and in accordance with the design quality management program.

· Providing Subject Matter Expert (SME) services as part of interdisciplinary pursuit teams working to develop innovative and cost-effective bid phase designs, identify key design risks, and develop plans to mitigate those risks.

· Coordinating with the Design and Project Management Team to ensure on-time and on-budget project delivery.

· Leading the exploration of alternate designs or new technologies to challenge the status quo and provoke exploration of new or innovative design solutions. Collaborating with staff and the Engineering Project Management Team to develop work scopes and labor estimates.

· Interfacing with Clients, Construction Personnel, Subconsultants, and Regulatory Agencies.

· Fostering an environment that emphasizes collaboration and coordination; providing feedback and encouraging learning to create growth opportunities; mentoring team members.

· Leading by example with respect to safety, quality, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

· Supervise and oversee the work of others as required.

Qualifications 

· Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Structural Engineering required. A master’s degree or PhD in Civil or Structural Engineering is preferred.

· 15+ years of progressively responsible structural engineering experience, preferably including hydropower, dams, hydraulic structures, heavy civil construction, and design-build project delivery.

· Hydraulic structures-focused experience including stability analyses; structural design of new hydraulic structures (concrete dams, hydropower stations, spillways, sluiceways, weirs, locks, levees, and related facilities); design of stability improvements to existing structures; condition assessment; structural design of repairs and refurbishments; and dam safety assessments.

· Experience working directly with contractors and construction teams through Early Contractor Involvement, Design-Build, Progressive Design-Build, or similar delivery models is preferred.

· Professional Engineer or equivalent registration in the applicable jurisdiction required or obtainable. An NCEES record is preferred for U.S.-based positions.

· Strong communication, collaboration, problem-solving, conflict-resolution, and organizational skills, with the ability to communicate effectively across all levels of the organization.

· Demonstrated autonomy, initiative, sound judgment, and ability to prioritize work while continuously improving quality, cost, safety, and efficiency and actively seeking feedback to improve processes.

· Knowledge of structural analysis and design software such as SAP2000, STAAD.Pro, SAFE, Mathcad, or equivalent tools.

· Experience working in a team setting and directing, reviewing, or mentoring the work of engineers and designers.

· Ability to travel to project sites and offices, generally less than 25 percent, and safely access construction sites in varying climates and environmental conditions.

#LI-JP1 

Working Conditions 

Other Requirements:
•    Regular, reliable attendance
•    Work productively and meet deadlines timely
•    Communicate and interact effectively and professionally with supervisors, employees, and others individually or in a team environment
•    Perform work safely and effectively. Understand and follow oral and written instructions, including warning signs, equipment use, and other policies.
•    Work during normal operating hours to organize and complete work within given deadlines. Work overtime and weekends as required.
•    May work at various different locations and conditions may vary.

jobs.title: Geotechnical Engineer, Dams and Hydraulic
jobs.summary: Kiewit is seeking a Geotechnical Engineer to support the analysis, design, and delivery of hydropower, dam, and hydraulic structure projects across North America.
jobs.description:
Requisition ID:  182015 

Job Level:  Mid Level 

Home District/Group:  Kiewit Infrastructure Engineers 

Department:  Design Engineering 

Market:  Power 

Employment Type:  Full Time 
 Position Overview 

Kiewit is seeking a Geotechnical Engineer to support the analysis, design, and delivery of hydropower, dam, and hydraulic structure projects across North America. This hands-on technical role focuses on engineering analyses and calculations, interpretation of geotechnical data, and preparation of practical designs, drawings, specifications, technical memoranda, and reports.

You will join Kiewit’s strong, experienced geotechnical team and work alongside multidisciplinary engineering teams, construction partners, and clients. Our geotechnical professionals are ready to mentor and support an eager engineer who wants to learn and grow, build sound technical judgment, and progressively take on greater technical, coordination, and leadership responsibilities.

Why Join Kiewit’s Hydropower & Dams Team? 

Work on large and/or complex hydropower and dam projects across Canada and the U.S.

Gain hands-on experience performing analyses and preparing practical designs that are built by Kiewit, with direct and continuous feedback from construction teams

Learn from a strong and supportive geotechnical team through active mentoring, technical reviews, field exposure, and knowledge sharing

Build experience across the project life cycle, from site investigation and design through construction support and multidisciplinary delivery

Develop technical and project leadership skills through progressively greater responsibility and support of the team’s technical and project leads

At Kiewit, we deliver some of the most challenging and meaningful infrastructure projects in North America. Our integrated design‑construction approach allows engineers to see their work built and to collaborate directly with construction teams to deliver innovative, practical solutions.

District Overview 

Kiewit Infrastructure Engineering seamlessly transitions solutions from design to construction through the collaborative efforts of Design Engineering, Design Management, Proposals, Estimating, and Integrated Project Controls. Our construction-focused engineering approach involves a multidisciplinary team working together to maximize value for clients by improving schedules, controlling costs, and minimizing risk on infrastructure projects. This integrated strategy emphasizes collaboration and constructability throughout the project lifecycle, enabling us to identify and implement quality solutions with a strong safety focus. 

Clients benefit from Kiewit’s proven processes and tools, which minimize project risk. As an in-house resource, we support projects across the company, in all major markets, sharing experiences, innovative concepts, and best practices. Kiewit’s management and implementation of this process result in safe, cost-effective, and innovative designs that exceed client expectations and uphold Kiewit’s legacy of excellence. 

At Kiewit, we believe in building more than just structures – we build relationships, strengthen communities, and expand workforce capacity. We don't just build projects; we build careers. With top-notch health benefits, a wealth-building 401k plan (RRSP), and unbeatable growth opportunities, we are deeply invested in the future of our employees. Join us at Kiewit, where we go beyond construction to develop the ultimate road to success. 

Location 

This position will be based out of Oakville, ON, with occasional travel as business necessitates to project sites and other offices (up to 15%).

Other Kiewit offices may be considered based on the candidate's experience.

Position could qualify for flexible remote work based on the candidate experience.

Responsibilities 

Geotechnical Analysis, Design & Reporting 

Review and interpret geological and geotechnical information, including borehole logs, field observations, laboratory test results, instrumentation data, design criteria, and previous studies.

Perform geotechnical and/or geological analyses and engineering calculations under the guidance of experienced engineers for foundations, embankments, slopes, underground works, and appurtenant structures.

Support evaluations of bearing capacity, settlement, slope and embankment stability, seepage, deformation, earth pressures, and seismic or liquefaction response, as applicable to each project.

Develop geotechnical parameters, assumptions, models, design criteria, and recommendations, clearly documenting their basis and limitations.

Prepare and organize calculation packages, design notes, technical memoranda, geotechnical reports, specifications, sketches, drawings, and other design deliverables.

Evaluate design alternatives and help develop safe, practical, and constructible solutions that meet project requirements and applicable codes and standards.

Coordinate with designers and multidisciplinary engineers to incorporate geotechnical analyses and recommendations into project drawings, models, and specifications.

Maintain clear and traceable design documentation, address technical review comments, and help improve design quality and efficiency through new tools and workflows, including responsible use of AI-enabled solutions.

Field & Construction Support 

Assist with geotechnical investigations, field data collection, sample and laboratory testing coordination, and documentation of site conditions.

Support instrumentation or monitoring programs, construction observations, and the organization and interpretation of field information.

Help evaluate differences between anticipated and encountered ground conditions and communicate relevant findings to the project team.

Assist project teams with requests for information, submittals, non-conformities, constructability concerns, and other technical issues under appropriate senior review.

Collaboration, Growth & Leadership Support 

Collaborate with civil, structural, hydraulic, mechanical, electrical, construction, and project controls personnel, as well as external design partners.

Support project and discipline leads with technical coordination, task planning, risk identification, schedule tracking, design reviews, and preparation for client, contractor, regulator, and stakeholder meetings.

As experience develops, coordinate defined technical tasks or small work packages, provide peer support to interns or less-experienced team members with senior guidance, and contribute to proposals, lessons learned, and practice-improvement initiatives.

Quality & Safety 

Complete work in accordance with Kiewit’s design quality management program, applicable professional standards, and project-specific requirements; perform self-checks and support independent reviews of calculations, drawings, specifications, and reports.

Actively support a collaborative culture focused on safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications 

Required 

Bachelor’s degree in Civil, Geological, Geotechnical, or a closely related engineering discipline.

Two to five years of relevant geotechnical engineering experience.

Registration, or eligibility for registration, with the engineering regulator in the province of employment, with a commitment to work toward professional licensure.

Experience performing or contributing to geotechnical analyses and calculations and preparing technical memoranda, reports, drawings, specifications, or other design deliverables.

Ability to interpret geotechnical investigation information, laboratory test results, field observations, and instrumentation or monitoring data.

Strong analytical, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.

Ability to work independently on clearly defined assignments while seeking guidance when appropriate and collaborating effectively within multidisciplinary teams.

Willingness to travel periodically to project offices and job sites.

Preferred (Not Required) 

Exposure to hydropower, dams, hydraulic structures, or other major water, energy, mining, transportation, or heavy civil infrastructure projects.

Master’s degree or PhD in a geotechnical or geological-related field.

Fluent in French and English (written and spoken).

Familiarity with relevant geotechnical analysis or numerical modelling software, data-analysis tools, CAD-based design workflows, or design automation.

Experience supporting site investigations, construction observations, instrumentation programs, or construction-phase activities.

Exposure to integrated or contractor-led delivery models such as Design-Build, EPC, or Progressive Design-Build.

Interest in constructability, AI-aided work-flows, design innovation, digital tools, professional development, and continuous improvement.

Interest in supporting other water or infrastructure markets part time as project needs and individual development interests align. #LI-GH 

Other Requirements:

Regular, reliable attendance

Work productively and meet deadlines timely

Communicate and interact effectively and professionally with supervisors, employees, and others individually or in a team environment

Perform work safely and effectively. Understand and follow oral and written instructions, including warning signs, equipment use, and other policies.

Work during normal operating hours to organize and complete work within given deadlines. Work overtime and weekends as required.

May work at various different locations and conditions may vary

Openings are to fill both existing vacancies and newly created positions 

Base Compensation: $95,000/yr - $100,000/yr
(Actual compensation is subject to variation due to such factors as education, experience, skillset, and/or location)

We offer our fulltime staff employees a comprehensive benefits package that’s among the best in our industry, including top-tier medical, dental and vision plans covering eligible employees and dependents, voluntary wellness and employee assistance programs, life insurance, disability, retirement plans with matching, and generous paid time off.

We believe in equal opportunity in employment practices without discrimination and comply with all laws regarding human rights in the provinces where we operate.

jobs.summary: We help clients navigate the complexities of climate change by developing strategies to mitigate risks and adapt to evolving conditions. We are seeking a strategic business and technical leader to…
jobs.description:
Requisition ID:  99957  

Job Category:  Environmental  

Location:  Essen, North Rhine, Germany  

Join a company that is passionately committed to the pursuit of a better world through positive change. With more than 70 years of business and technical expertise in mining , energy , and infrastructure , our 10,000 colleagues in 150 countries tirelessly work toward bettering the industries in which we operate. With practical solutions that are safe, innovative and sustainable, we think globally while acting locally. Are you looking for an opportunity to join a diverse group of professionals who are committed to remaining exceptional? We look forward to hearing from you. 

We help clients navigate the complexities of climate change by developing strategies to mitigate risks and adapt to evolving conditions. Our scientific, evidence-based approach drives resilient solutions that safeguard communities, assets, and ecosystems for the future. 

We are seeking a strategic business and technical leader to help grow Hatch's Climate Change practice across Europe and the UK. This role is responsible for driving business development, leading multidisciplinary engineering and consulting teams, managing project delivery, and supporting clients across the metals, energy, and infrastructure sectors. The successful candidate will combine strong commercial acumen, engineering leadership, and climate change expertise to help clients navigate decarbonization, climate risk, resilience, and the transition to a low-carbon future.  

In this role you will: 

Help lead Hatch’s climate change consulting and engineering services in Europe and the UK. 

Drive regional growth, team development, and financial performance 

Lead business development activities across the European region 

Build and maintain client relationships across metals, energy, and infrastructure sectors in decarbonization and resilience 

Collaborate with regional business unit and business practice teams on external and internal climate change activities 

Lead engagements related to climate-related disclosures, decarbonization planning, climate policy, carbon markets, low-carbon products, and climate risk 

Manage engineering studies related to carbon and energy management, electrification, biochar and biocarbon, hydrogen, carbon capture, carbon dioxide removal, and adaptation 

Seek out opportunities to communicate Hatch’s differentiated service offerings and represent Hatch in conferences and other client-facing opportunities 

What you bring:  

Minimum 15 years of experience in engineering leadership, project management, technical consulting, and business development. 

Demonstrated success leading multidisciplinary teams and delivering complex capital project studies and engineering projects. 

Proven ability to develop client relationships, generate opportunities, and grow regional business performance. 

Experience leading technical teams across geographically distributed and global organizations.

jobs.title: Coordinator - Environmental
jobs.summary: The Environmental Coordinator is accountable for the day-to-day coordination of site-based environmental management activities for the Future Generation Joint Venture delivering Snowy 2.0, to ensure…
jobs.description:
The Future Generation Joint Venture brings together the combined engineering experience and expertise of WeBuild, Clough and Lane and has been selected to design construct Snowy 2.0 . This project is based within the Snowy Mountains in NSW and will deliver one of the largest pumped hydro schemes in the world.  

Snowy 2.0 is the next chapter in the Snowy Scheme's history. It is the largest committed renewable energy project in Australia and will provide on-demand energy and large-scale storage for many generations to come. This Iconic Project has and will continue to create its own legacy in Australian history. 

Purpose of the Role 

The Environmental Coordinator is accountable for the day-to-day coordination of site-based environmental management activities and construction team support to ensure that Future Generation Joint Venture (FGJV) maintains a robust Environmental Management System in accordance with the approved Environmental Protection Licence, Conditions of Consent, Environmental Management Strategy and associated Environmental Management Plans (EMPs) and client specifications. 

Qualifications 

Tertiary qualifications in environmental management or a related discipline

Minimum class C driver licence

White Card

Experience 

Minimum 5 years of experience working in the construction industry in a similar role preferred 

Experience in the development and implementation of environmental management systems and plans 

Interpretation and implementation of environmental programs to ensure compliance with environmental approval conditions and environmental management systems 

Experience working on large scale construction projects or other suitable project works 

Demonstrated experience managing teams on environmentally sensitive projects 

Required Competencies 

Ability to build sound working relationships with clients and colleagues

Ability to coach and mentor

Ability to work to deadlines and targets

Ability to effectively prioritise and make confident decisions

Strong initiative, organisational skills and attention to detail

Ability to maintain focus and deliver outcomes in dynamic or challenging situations while adapting to changing priorities

Sound negotiation skills

Capability to lead teams effectively and maintain a productive work environment during periods of high workload or organisational change

Ability to work autonomously as well as collaboratively with on-site construction teams

Fundamental understanding of ISO AS/NZS 14001

Commitment and proactive approach to site safety processes and practices

Effective analytical and communication skills, including report writing

Core Accountabilities and Responsibilities 

Provide advice and support to the site construction management team to ensure compliance with statutory, FGJV and client environmental obligations.

Implement and develop environmental plans and subsidiary systems documentation as required.

Communicate HSSE issues and standards.

Support the site environment team and ensure they are properly resourced to meet all relevant environmental obligations.

Assist in identifying environmental training requirements.

Analyse and report FGJV lead (LPI’s) and lag (incident reporting) targets to Project Management.

Review changes to design or methodologies affecting environment or sustainability and ensure they are captured in risk assessments, Job Safety Environmental Analyses (JSEAs) or Safe Work Method Statements (SWMSs) as required.

Ensure all incident events and investigations are properly conducted, recorded and information closed out in accordance with FGJV reporting timeframes.

Escalate critical environmental issues.

Promote a dynamic and positive QHSSE culture focused on achieving success.

Coach and mentor Environmental Advisors.

Manage environmental sub-contractors.

Manage and coordinate all environmental actions raised.

Draft regulatory response letters and reports as required.

Support all environmental audits as required.

Lead the site Environmental Technical Assistants.

Ensure representation is maintained at key construction planning and coordination meetings.

Undertake additional tasks, as directed by Environmental Management/Superintendent to support FGJV’s Project HSSE goals and values.

The above listed authorities and responsibilities are only a guide and may change as directed by your Manager/Supervisor or as per the requirements of FGJV Management. 

As an employee you will be eligible to participate in a number of additional employee benefits .  This includes: 

Competitive Salary 

Employee Assistance Program (EAP) 

Paid Parental Leave 

Qantas Club Membership discounts 

Professional Development 

The employment relationship will be governed by Australia or New Zealand Employment Law. 

These positions are in remote challenging areas with extreme cold temperatures which need to be considered before applying for these roles.  

If you meet the above requirements and would like to work on this iconic project, please apply now.

jobs.title: Survey Manager - Kiewit Offshore Services
jobs.summary: As a Survey Manager at KOS, you will play an integral role in establishing and maintaining methods for safe, accurate and efficient Survey/Dimensional Control operations.
jobs.description:
Requisition ID:  182929 

Job Level:  Mid Level 

Home District/Group:  Kiewit Offshore Services District 

Department:  Surveying 

Market:  OGC 

Employment Type:  Full Time 

Position Overview 

As a Survey Manager at KOS, you will play an integral role in establishing and maintaining methods for safe, accurate and efficient Survey/Dimensional Control operations. You will have responsibilities over field survey operations, and should plan to spend the majority of your time in the field performing surveying operations. 

District Overview 

Kiewit Offshore Services, a district (or business unit) of Kiewit Corporation that builds structurally complex jackets and topsides for offshore oil drilling rigs. Located in Ingleside, TX, 20 minutes outside of Corpus Christi, the 550-acre fabrication yard is the workplace of 300 staff employees and 1400 craft employees who work in the yard year-round. The projects built by Kiewit Offshore Services require significant equipment planning, detailed cost estimates and schedules, a commitment to safety by all employees, and are truly unforgettable. The Kiewit Offshore Services team is a diverse, tight knit group that enjoys fun team building events such as deep-sea fishing, golfing, and sporting events throughout the year. The employees are extremely schedule driven, high-energy, friendly, and hard workers.

Within the Oil, Gas & Chemical Industry, their teams are the best evidenced by the countless project opportunities from owners who seek their expertise when challenged with complex projects. Kiewit Offshore Service leaders are seeking employees who would enjoy living in Southern Texas, ready for a fast-paced career, trainable, and can work well within a diverse team.

Location 

This position will be initially based out of Kiewit Offshore Services Ingleside, TX location.

Responsibilities 

Field computations

Maintain accurate, detailed and legible field notes.

Utilization of Leica Total Station

Team management

Ensures that project/department milestones/goals are met and adhering to approved budgets

Qualifications 

At least 1+ years' experience in Dimensional Control, Industrial Measurement, Construction Survey, or a related field is required

GPS experience is a plus

Strong computer skills (excel/word)

Must be able to apply concepts of basic algebra and geometry to perform calculations (area, volume, circumference, proportion, percentage)

Dynamic thinker with the desire to lead, motivate and mentor teams

Self-starter with the ability to set standards of excellence in leadership, safety, quality and productivity

Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Strong work ethic with the ability to work individually and as a team

Committed to working safe and getting the job done right the first time

#LI-HW1 

Other Requirements: 

•    Regular, reliable attendance

•    Work productively and meet deadlines timely

•    Communicate and interact effectively and professionally with supervisors, employees, and others individually or in a team environment.

•    Perform work safely and effectively. Understand and follow oral and written instructions, including warning signs, equipment use, and other policies.

•    Work during normal operating hours to organize and complete work within given deadlines. Work overtime and weekends as required.

We offer our fulltime staff employees a comprehensive benefits package that’s among the best in our industry, including top-tier medical, dental and vision plans covering eligible employees and dependents, voluntary wellness and employee assistance programs, life insurance, disability, retirement plans with matching, and generous paid time off.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

jobs.title: Design Survey Manager - Kiewit Infrastructure Engineers
jobs.summary: Kiewit Infrastructure Engineers (KIE) is looking for a Survey Manager to join our Design Survey Team, helping Kiewit's Design Build group by coordinating and managing KIE's survey vendors during the…
jobs.description:
Requisition ID:  182935 

Job Level:  Senior Level 

Home District/Group:  Kiewit Infrastructure Engineers 

Department:  Surveying 

Market:  Transportation 

Employment Type:  Full Time 

Position Overview 

Kiewit Infrastructure Engineers (KIE) is looking for a Survey Manager to join our Design Survey Team. This job position will help Kiewit’s Design Build group by coordinating and managing KIE’s survey vendors during the design phase. The candidate will have sufficient experience to support this Subject Matter Expert (SME) position and be familiar with current surveying and mapping best practices regarding survey collection utilizing traditional surveying methods as well as LiDAR and other technologies. The Design Survey Team is responsible for survey & mapping data acquisition used by the Engineering Design Team within KIE. Our services ensure the design survey collection meets the design schedule and follows Kiewit’s quality standards.

District Overview 

Kiewit Infrastructure Engineering's Design-Build team is driving clients to turn to Kiewit during all stages of design-build projects.  Through our integrated design and construction approach, our multi-disciplinary team works together to improve schedule, control costs and minimize risk.  Our construction-focused engineers work collaboratively with our estimators and builders to design solutions that are innovative, constructible, and designed with a focus on safety.   Clients benefit from the proven processes and tools used by Kiewit to minimize project risk. We are an in-house resource that supports projects throughout the company. Our staff shares experiences gained, innovative concepts, and best practices for all projects that we support.

Kiewit’s management and implementation of this process leads to safe, cost effective, and innovative designs that exceeds client expectations and furthers Kiewit’s legacy of excellence.

On our team, you’ll have the opportunity to see more, touch more, and do more than you ever imagined. Working hard will not only bring you satisfaction from a job well done, but it will help propel your career forward faster than you might expect. We will train you, develop your skills, and allow you to take on projects that impact millions across North America. With top-notch health benefits, a wealth-building 401k plan, and unbeatable growth opportunities, by joining Kiewit, you’re ensuring a lifetime of success.

Location 

This position can be based in the following KIE offices: 
- Lone Tree, CO
- Bellevue, WA
- Westlake, TX
- Woodcliff Lake, NJ
- New York, NY

Responsibilities 

•    Review client Request for Proposal (RFP) documents to identify the estimating and design survey needs.
•    Prepare RFP packets for third-party survey vendors ensuring all necessary deliverables and deadlines are clearly communicated.
•    Evaluate responses to proposals and prepare recommendations to the project team based on project needs including skill level, cost, availability, and licensing. 
•    Work with our corporate business group to create Master Service Agreements and Task Orders for the required work.
•    Be the onsite representative to the third-party vendor as they perform their work to ensure they are operating in accordance with Kiewit’s Safety procedures.
•    Act as a liaison between third-party vendor and KIE’s Existing Conditions Team.
•    Ensure the Quality Control procedures are followed to verify the data is delivered accurately and on-time.
•    Review and coordinate all design survey requests with the selected vendor to meet the design schedule and expectations. 

Qualifications 

•    Active Professional Land Surveyor License (PLS, PS, LS, PSM, RLS) or LSIT certification in any state preferred but not required
•    10+ years combined experience: Design Survey and Construction Survey.
•    5+ years Lidar exposure (Terrestrial, Mobile, Aerial), collection background.
•    Travel up to 50% of the time.
•    Strong knowledge of State Plane coordinate systems (grid vs. ground).
•    Survey background in both office and field operations. 
•    Experience with one or more of the following surveying/design software at an intermediate level such as Trimble Business Center, Bentley Microstation (InRoads/OpenRoads Designer) or Autodesk Civil 3D is required.
•    Understanding of drone surveying applications is required 
•    Must have advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite.
•    Self-starter with the ability to set standards of excellence in leadership, safety, quality, and productivity.
•    Strong attention to details and problem solving/analytical skills.
•    Excellent communication is a must.
•    Strong work ethic with the ability to work individually and as a team.
•    Able to carry up to 50lb.

#LI-JT1 

Other Requirements:
•    Regular, reliable attendance
•    Work productively and meet deadlines timely
•    Communicate and interact effectively and professionally with supervisors, employees, and others individually or in a team environment
•    Perform work safely and effectively. Understand and follow oral and written instructions, including warning signs, equipment use, and other policies.
•    Work during normal operating hours to organize and complete work within given deadlines. Work overtime and weekends as required.

Base Compensation: $126,000/yr - $150,000/yr 
(Actual compensation is subject to variation due to such factors as education, experience, skillset, and/or location)

This posting will be active from:    10/30/2026  - 03/01/2027  

We offer our fulltime staff employees a comprehensive benefits package that’s among the best in our industry, including top-tier medical, dental and vision plans covering eligible employees and dependents, voluntary wellness and employee assistance programs, life insurance, disability, retirement plans with matching, and generous paid time off.

Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status.

jobs.description:
Requisition ID:  180336 

Job Level:  Mid Level 

Home District/Group:  Kiewit Infrastructure Engineers 

Department:  Design Engineering 

Market:  Transportation 

Employment Type:  Full Time 

Position Overview 

The Concrete Engineer is a team member of Kiewit Infrastructure Engineering  (KIE).  This position’s primary role is to provide support to construction oprerations, perform analysis, and design to Kiewit projects, including a direct impact to other teams within the engineering district.  

Project involvement of a concrete engineer can be at any stage (Get Work or Build Work) of a project’s life cycle.  Get Work project tasks can include proposal development, Task Force participation, technical proposal design including alternative technical design concept (ATC), and proposal cost estimating support.  Build Work project tasks can include Task Force participation, development of final designs including but not limited to concrete troubleshooting, development of project specifications, concrete mixes, testing procedures, preparations of thermal control plans, durability and service life engineering, construction engineering, and construction operations oversight.  

Projects often rely on KIE technical resources, consultants, and/or subcontractors for staffing engineering related construction tasks.  Typical project deliverables may include technical solutions, design reports, memorandums, and letters.  These deliverables provide technical analysis, technical interpretations, and professional recommendations; all these project deliverables are subject to KIE’s Design Quality Management Plan. Project deliverables may require field technical support with investigations and site visit observations during project construction.

Concrete Engineering is considered a “specialty” engineering service and as such has high visibility with Project upper management where high professionalism is always expected.  Project related travel varies but it is projected to be approximately 25% and it can be anywhere in North America. Continued job related learning (Kiewit University, Professional Engineer Continued Education, personal professional development) is encouraged and expected.

District Overview 

2025 ENR National Contractor Rankings #1 for Transportation and #3 Top 100 design build firms  

Kiewit Infrastructure Engineers seamlessly transitions solutions from design to construction through the collaborative efforts of Design Engineering, Design Management, Proposals, Estimating, and Integrated Project Controls. Our construction-focused engineering approach involves a multidisciplinary team working together to maximize value for clients by improving schedules, controlling costs, and minimizing risk on infrastructure projects. This integrated strategy emphasizes collaboration and constructability throughout the project lifecycle, enabling us to identify and implement quality solutions with a strong safety focus.

Clients benefit from Kiewit’s proven processes and tools, which minimize project risk. As an in-house resource, we support projects across the company, in all major markets, sharing experiences, innovative concepts, and best practices. Kiewit’s management and implementation of this process result in safe, cost-effective, and innovative designs that exceed client expectations and uphold Kiewit’s legacy of excellence.

At Kiewit, we believe in building more than just structures – we build relationships, strengthen communities, and expand workforce capacity. We don't just build projects; we build careers. With top-notch health benefits, a wealth-building 401k plan (RRSP), and unbeatable growth opportunities, we are deeply invested in the future of our employees. Join us at Kiewit, where we go beyond construction to develop the ultimate road to success.

Location 

This position is based out of our Westlake, TX office.

Responsibilities 

Assist the Chief Concrete Engineer in providing and managing concrete technical solutions

Support with pre-bid evaluation, design constructability reviews, technical risk assessments and construction operations work planning (i.e., placing procedures, pumping, constructability reviews, mix design, value engineering, troubleshooting, proposal development, and training.)

Assist in improving concrete quality and reducing concrete quality issues through proactive engagement with Jobsite personnel.

Collaborate in developing concrete related design requirements and specifications for construction

Interpret concrete materials properties and construction quality results including process control data 

Serve as field engineer during construction when interest and opportunities align

Interpret/learn/apply client specific design methodologies, specifications, and standards 

Develop and maintain internal and external client relationships and construction partners, including project and non-project related face-to-face meetings

Qualifications 

B.S. degree in Civil Engineering. Master’s degree with emphasis in concrete or related engineering field preferred. 

Minimum of 7 years of experience directly applicable to concrete (including mix designs, thermal control analysis, service life engineering, forensic analysis, troubleshooting, technical requirements, testing procedures, applicable codes,  standards and best practices, ACI manual of concrete practice, etc.)

Active US PE required

Ability to travel in North America (expected travel approximately 25%)

Must be proficient in the Microsoft Office suite of products

Knowledgeable in concrete industry standards, such as ASTM, ACI and CSA 

Experience with industry specific software analysis and design software, with emphasis related to concrete mixture proportioning, thermal modeling, and service life analysis

Proficient written and verbal communication skills

Do you have experience with agentic AI, such as using AI agents or agentic workflows to plan and execute tasks?

#LI-JP1 

Working Conditions 

Other Requirements:

Regular, reliable attendance 

Work productively and meet deadlines timely

Communicate and interact effectively and professionally with supervisors, employees, and others individually or in a team environment.

Perform work safely and effectively. Understand and follow oral and written instructions, including warning signs, equipment use, and other policies.

Work during normal operating hours to organize and complete work within given deadlines. Work overtime and weekends as required.

May work at various different locations and conditions may vary.

We offer our fulltime staff employees a comprehensive benefits package that’s among the best in our industry, including top-tier medical, dental and vision plans covering eligible employees and dependents, voluntary wellness and employee assistance programs, life insurance, disability, retirement plans with matching, and generous paid time off.

Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status.

jobs.description:
Requisition ID:  97629 

Job Category:  Infrastructure 

Location:  Brisbane, Queensland, Australia 

Join a company that is passionately committed to the pursuit of a better world through positive change. With more than 65 years of business and technical expertise in  mining , energy , and infrastructure , our 10,000 colleagues in 150 countries tirelessly work toward bettering the industries in which we operate. With practical solutions that are safe, innovative and sustainable, we think globally while acting locally. Are you looking for an opportunity to join a diverse group of professionals who are committed to remaining exceptional? We look forward to hearing from you.

Our expertise in infrastructure includes aviation, highways and bridges, planning and advisory services, ports, rail and transit, tunnels, and water. Want to be part of the creation and construction of our cities? Then the infrastructure team is for you!

Our Brisbane Infrastructure team is entering an exciting growth phase, driven by newly awarded high‑profile projects and forward‑thinking workforce planning. As a result, we’re looking for a  Senior Highways Engineer  to play a key role in delivering major transport projects within our multi‑disciplinary consultancy. You’ll bring strong experience in the roads and highways sector, particularly with DTMR, and apply both your technical expertise and leadership capability to help strengthen and expand our Roads & Highways team.

This is a rare opportunity to join a business on the rise where your technical influence, project leadership, and collaborative mindset will directly shape our future. You’ll work alongside talented professionals across disciplines, contribute to the growth of the practice, and elevate your career as part of Hatch’s broader communities of practice. 

Key responsibilities of your role will include: 

Supervising civil engineering design for freeways, intersections, bulk earthworks, roads and rail

Preparing, reviewing and checking engineering calculations, technical specifications, data sheets and reports

Reviewing and checking engineering drawings

Providing input to engineering, operating and cost estimates

Leading in and contributing to design reviews

Leading designs from tender through feasibility to detailed design

Client/Stakeholder management

Managing commercial aspects of projects

Assisting with bidding and tenders

Mentoring junior staff

About you: 

The ideal candidate will have proven experience coordinating, designing, and delivering road projects in Queensland for DTMR as part of multi‑disciplinary teams, supported by a civil engineering degree from a recognised tertiary institution. They will demonstrate strong safety awareness, excellent communication and interpersonal skills, and a collaborative, inclusive approach to working with others. Their technical background will include expertise in bulk earthworks, site grading, surface water management, access and haul roads, freeways, and earth structures. Registration as an RPEQ or CPEng will be highly regarded.

Why join us? 

Work with great people to make a difference

Collaborate on exciting projects to develop innovative solutions

Top employer 

What we offer you? 

Global project exposure across complex, impactful industries

Strong focus on career growth, learning and mentorship

Collaborative, values-driven culture focused on innovation and excellence

Don't meet every single requirement? You don't need to. At Hatch, we are building a diverse, inclusive workplace that fosters innovation. If you're interested in this role, we encourage you to apply even if your past experiences don't perfectly align with the skills we've listed.

Hatch holds an innovate reconciliation action plan and we encourage Aboriginal and Torres Straight islanders to apply. As an accredited Employer of Choice for Gender Equality (WGEA) and Equal Opportunity Employer, we are committed to fostering a workforce in each of our locations that reflects the diversity of the communities in which we operate. Within Australia, this includes supporting and encouraging a collaborative workplace and a comprehensive benefit offering. If you have any special needs requirements, please discuss with us and we will do our utmost to accommodate your request. We are managing this recruitment process directly and are not accepting unsolicited resumes from recruitment agencies.

 Civil Engineer, Construction, Sustainability, Engineer, Engineering, Energy, Aviation

Job Level:  Mid Level 

Home District/Group:  Kiewit Infrastructure Engineers 

Department:  Design Engineering 

Market:  Transportation 

Employment Type:  Full Time 
 Position Overview 

Kiewit Infrastructure Engineering (KIE) is currently seeking a Traffic Engineer in our growing Design Group in Burnaby, BC.  You will be part of our rapidly growing Infrastructure Design Department, which includes structural, geotechnical, roadway, maintenance of traffic (MOT), civil, drainage, and rail disciplines, a multi-faceted and leading-edge division of Kiewit with best-in-class technical expertise focused on the design-build delivery of infrastructure projects.  As a Traffic Engineer with MOT focus, the successful candidate will prepare MOT plans, coordinate with engineering and construction staff, and ensure our roadway designs are safe and efficient.  You will be expected to coordinate with project teams in Canada and the United States to design and produce traffic engineering and MOT designs for design/build projects in North America.

2025 ENR National Contractor Rankings #1 for Transportation and #3 Top 100 design build firms 

Kiewit Infrastructure Engineering's Design-Build team is driving clients to turn to Kiewit during all stages of design-build projects. Through our integrated design and construction approach, our multi-disciplinary team works together to improve schedule, control costs and minimize risk.  Our construction-focused engineers work collaboratively with our estimators and builders to design solutions that are innovative, constructible, and designed with a focus on safety. Clients benefit from the proven processes and tools used by Kiewit to minimize project risk. We are an in-house resource that supports projects throughout the company. Our staff shares experiences gained, innovative concepts, and best practices for all projects that we support.

Kiewit’s management and implementation of this process leads to safe, cost effective, and innovative designs that exceeds client expectations and furthers Kiewit’s legacy of excellence.

On our team, you’ll have the opportunity to see more, touch more, and do more than you ever imagined. jobs.description:
Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

Role description:

Arcadis is seeking a entry-level Environmental Engineer to join our established, multi-disciplinary team in our Indianapolis, IN office. This is an entry-level opportunity for a motivated individual looking for career growth in the environmental consulting field. May 2027 graduates are encouraged to apply. 

As part of our Resilience Environment team, you’ll help improve quality of life. 

Role accountabilities:

The position offers an opportunity to learn about a wide variety of environmental projects, work with a talented team of professionals/mentors, and join a successful growing organization with a reputation for high-quality work and helping its world-class clients solve their most challenging issues. Arcadis provides multiple onboarding and development programs created for our young professionals that will expand professional growth and help drive creativeness, innovation, and greater integration within our local, national, and global teams.

Your responsibilities may include the following: 

* Perform fieldwork in all weather conditions which may include drilling oversight for soil sampling and/or groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, excavation oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, and vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys
 * Coordination, management, reduction, and evaluation of field and analytical data as a key part in the preparation of technical deliverables
 * Assist Project Managers (PMs) and Assistant PMs (APMs) with planning environmental investigation and remediation tasks
 * Exhibit ownership of delegated tasks, including responsibility for coordination and delivery of on-schedule and on-budget tasks
 * Office work may include task coordination, technical reports, data compilation, analysis, and interpretation, cost estimates, health & safety plan preparation, report writing, regulatory file review, permitting activities, proposal writing, project specifications & strategy development, scheduling, and cost estimating.
 * Environmental remediation design tasks, including soil and groundwater remedial system and in-situ technology treatment design and assessment
 * Interpretation and evaluation of field and analytical data to prepare engineering designs, permit applications, and construction-related documents

This is a full-time entry-level position that requires attention to detail, strong work ethic, excellent written and verbal communication skills, and willingness to perform field work. This position is expected to support various projects from environmental investigation through design, permitting and remediation. The successful candidate will be working alongside and supporting task managers, technical experts, and project managers on multiple projects. Responsibilities will include a combination of field and office related tasks and will include travel and field work. 

During some periods, field work is expected to be as much as 60 to 80 percent of the candidate’s time with some travel requiring hotel stays. Field work may be performed at project sites with environmental media (e.g., soil, sediment, groundwater, surface water, etc.) that has been impacted with hazardous substances and/or hazardous wastes.

Fieldwork is a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks. Additionally, Arcadis supports many of our client’s needs when unforeseen incidents occur, such as train derailments, pipeline releases, etc. An aspect of this role is supporting our National emergency response teams to ensure rapid protection of human health and the environment. This work is completed under the direction of trained incident responders and may require unanticipated travel and work outside standard business hours.

Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time. Estimated travel is up to 75% during the first two years, with travel reduced with career growth. By the third year, travel for field work is typically 50%. Travel expenses are reimbursable. 

Qualifications & Experience:

Required Qualifications

* Undergraduate degree in Engineering (Environmental, Civil, Chemical, or closely related field)

Preferred Qualifications 

* 40-hour OSHA HAZWOPER training and appropriate annual refresher certifications
 * Power BI experience
 * 1 year experience
 * Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification preferred

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We are an equal opportunity employer. We are dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on any basis including race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, disability, veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

Arcadis offers benefits for full time and part time positions. These benefits include medical, dental, and vision, EAP, 401K, STD, LTD, AD&D, life insurance, paid parental leave, reward & recognition program and optional benefits including wellbeing benefits, adoption assistance and tuition reimbursement. We offer nine paid holidays and 15 days PTO that accrue per year. The salary range for this position is $54,648- $81,972. Actual salaries will vary and are based on several factors, such as experience, education, budget, internal equity, project and location.

 At Aurecon, we are engineering optimists who see the world differently. We ask what’s possible and turn ideas into impact.  Here, you’ll bring your expertise to challenges that matter, alongside people who think boldly and are determined to make a difference.

You’ll guide teams across complex delivery environments, balancing competing priorities, risks and constraints whilst driving strong delivery performance.

Also, a thorough understanding in road design using 12D software with strong knowledge of data transfer between key software packages. Manage project design teams (designers and drafters), and work collaboratively with project managers, engineers and other discipline leads to deliver quality products within agreed time and budget.

 ·         Lead integrated technical delivery across workstreams, ensuring quality outputs.   
 ·         Prepare design models, suitable for digital issue to our end client and for construction purposes. Demonstrated knowledge in BIM is one of the key aspects. 
 ·         Able to work in major projects under joint venture environment and lead road design modelling work.
 ·         Manage and mentor junior staff. 
 ·         Involvement in development of digital strategy for our Roads and Highways team and be part of our computational design team. 
 ·         Lead client interactions to influence decisions and maintain delivery alignment.  
 How we support your growth 
 Engineering possibilities for your career means having room to shape what comes next. You bring your ambition and commitment to lifelong learning, and we provide the foundation and development to help you turn your aspirations into achievement.
 The Aurecon Way guides how we think, act and work together, what we value and how we invest in our people. You’ll be part of a culture built on clear expectations, optimism and determination, where you can feel safe, included and empowered to speak openly, think boldly and deliver brilliantly.
 Who we are 
 We are an engineering consultancy with more than 6,000 people across Australia, New Zealand and Asia. We believe the world needs people who can engineer possibilities; people who can create infrastructure that makes life better for people and the planet. That is why we are here – to bring ideas to life, the Aurecon way.
 Ready to engineer possibilities?

jobs.description:
Civil Engineer 

At Aurecon, we are engineering optimists who see the world differently. We ask what’s possible and turn ideas into impact.  Here, you’ll bring your expertise to challenges that matter, alongside people who think boldly and are determined to make a difference.

What You’ll Do

As a Civil Engineer in our Industrial, Mining & Resources team based in Brisbane , you'll take on industrial, mining and resources, ports, energy and oil & gas projects, helping shape solutions for our clients and communities. 

You’ll work across disciplines, test ideas and find better ways to solve complex engineering problems. You will:

Contribute to civil studies and designs across bulk earthworks, drainage, pavements, underground services and site infrastructure.
 Coordinate geotechnical inputs and civil interfaces to help develop integrated and constructable design solutions.
 Support projects from concept and feasibility through detailed design, construction support and sustainment works.
 Work alongside multidisciplinary engineering teams to solve technical challenges across complex industrial environments.
 Build your client-facing capability by translating technical information into clear, practical engineering advice.

Your experience and expertise 

Relevant Civil Engineering qualification and up to 5 years’ experience, ideally with some exposure to civil design, consulting, construction or industrial infrastructure.
 A foundation in, or genuine interest in developing your career within Industrial Civil engineering.
 An interest in areas such as earthworks, drainage, pavements, underground services and multidisciplinary site infrastructure.
 A practical approach to developing solutions that balance technical quality, constructability and client outcomes.
 Strong communication and collaboration skills, with an eagerness to learn from experienced technical specialists.

For someone early in their career, this is an opportunity to build broad Industrial Civil capability, rather than being limited to one type of project, with exposure to different sectors, disciplines and stages of the engineering lifecycle.

How we support your growth 

Engineering possibilities for your career means having room to shape what comes next. You bring your ambition and commitment to lifelong learning, and we provide the foundation and development to help you turn your aspirations into achievement.

The Aurecon Way guides how we think, act and work together, what we value and how we invest in our people. You’ll be part of a culture built on clear expectations, optimism and determination, where you can feel safe, included and empowered to speak openly, think boldly and deliver brilliantly.

Who we are 

We are an engineering consultancy with more than 6,000 people across Australia, New Zealand and Asia. We believe the world needs people who can engineer possibilities; people who can create infrastructure that makes life better for people and the planet. That is why we are here – to bring ideas to life, the Aurecon way.

Ready to engineer possibilities? 

If this sounds like your next step, we’d love to hear from you. We value diverse experiences and welcome applications for part-time or flexible working arrangements. For recruitment adjustments, contact WorkplaceAdjustment@aurecongroup.com.

Our hiring decisions are made by people, not AI. We’re interested in your thinking and experience, so please ensure your application reflects your authentic perspective.

jobs.description:
KCB is a multidisciplinary engineering, geoscience, and environmental consulting firm grounded in our values of Passion, Integrity, and Excellence. With teams across North America, South America, Australasia, and Europe, we bring together global technical knowledge, local insight, and a shared commitment to solving complex challenges that matter.

Guided by our long-term ambition of Globally Connected Excellence and our purpose of Sustaining the Future, we work alongside our clients to deliver lasting solutions that strengthen resilience and benefit future generations.

Who We're Looking For

We're growing our Brisbane Geotechnical Engineering team and are seeking a Senior Geotechnical Engineer to help deliver technically complex projects across tailings and mine waste storage facilities, water management structures, dams, and mining infrastructure.

In this role, you'll leverage your technical expertise, leadership capability, and relationship-building skills to lead the delivery of significant tailings, dam, mine waste, and geotechnical projects across Australia and internationally. You'll also play a key role in strengthening existing client relationships, developing new business opportunities, and expanding KCB's presence throughout the region.

We're looking for a respected consulting engineer with a strong technical reputation and a proven ability to help clients solve complex engineering challenges. The successful candidate will be comfortable leading multidisciplinary teams, engaging directly with clients, providing technical oversight and mentorship, and contributing to strategic project and business development initiatives.

This opportunity is ideal for someone who is motivated by technical excellence, values long-term client partnerships, and is excited by the opportunity to help shape the continued growth and success of KCB's Australian business.

What You'll do

As a Senior Geotechnical Engineer, you will:

- Lead and contribute to the planning, design, assessment, and management of tailings storage facilities, mine waste facilities, water storage dams, and associated earthworks infrastructure.

- Provide senior technical leadership and review for complex geotechnical, tailings, and dam engineering projects.

- For the right candidate with appropriate experience, fulfill Engineer of Record roles for operational facilities as part of a larger technical project team.

- Undertake and oversee:

- Slope stability assessments

- Seepage and groundwater analyses

- Tailings deposition modelling

- Dam safety and risk assessments

- Closure and rehabilitation planning

- Material characterisation and interpretation of laboratory and field investigation data

- Lead geotechnical investigations, field programs, site inspections, construction monitoring, and QA/QC activities.

- Prepare and review technical reports, design documentation, specifications, proposals, and engineering studies.

- Manage multidisciplinary project teams to deliver projects safely, efficiently, and to a high technical standard.

- Provide project management leadership including planning, budgeting, scheduling, resource coordination, and contract management.

- Develop and maintain strong relationships with existing and prospective clients.

- Identify, pursue, and help secure new business opportunities across the mining, resources, and water sectors.

- Lead or contribute to proposals, tenders, and contract negotiations.

- Mentor and coach graduate, junior, and intermediate engineers, supporting their professional development and technical growth.

- Promote technical excellence, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement across the business.

- Work in accordance with KCB's Quality Management System and Health & Safety requirements.

- Collaborate with teams across Australia and KCB's global network.

What You'll Bring
