jobs.description:
SENIOR GEOTECHNICAL ENGINEER – Lead ground control at Australia's most exciting emerging gold-antimony project

5:2 Roster | Full-time, Permanent | Sunday Creek, VIC (residential) Underground Development

SXGC is exploring the most exciting new gold and antimony discovery in Australia, with our flagship Sunday Creek project moving from surface exploration towards future underground mining. As the operation grows, strong ground control will keep our people and workings safe while supporting efficient underground development and stoping, so we're looking for a Senior Geotechnical Engineer to lead that function and build the team behind it.

Why SXGC?

Because your work here matters.

You'll join a growing ASX and TSX-listed explorer at a pivotal stage, leading geotechnical engineering as Sunday Creek moves from exploration towards development. Here your work matters on the ground: you'll set the ground control standards, systems and team that underground mining at Sunday Creek will rely on, working closely with the mining, development and projects teams.

About the Role

Reporting to the Underground Development Manager, you will lead geotechnical engineering at Sunday Creek to keep people and workings safe from ground-related hazards while supporting efficient underground development and stoping. You'll own the Ground Control Management Plan, ground support design and standards, geotechnical monitoring and data, and excavation and stope design input. You'll lead Geotechnical Engineers and Technicians, manage geotechnical consultants and ground support contractors, and provide geotechnical leadership to the mining, development and projects teams, with input to studies as the operation grows.

What You’ll Drive

Lead and develop the geotechnical team, including Geotechnical Engineers and Technicians, building a strong ground-awareness and safety culture across site

Own and maintain the Ground Control Management Plan and the ground-related principal mining hazard controls under the site Safety Management System

Design ground support for development, stoping and infrastructure excavations, and set and maintain ground support standards and Trigger Action Response Plans (TARPs)

Provide geotechnical input to mine design, including stope dimensions, pillar design, sequencing, backfill requirements and excavation stability, using numerical and empirical methods

Manage geotechnical data collection, rock mass characterisation and core logging, and maintain the site geotechnical model and database

Plan and run geotechnical monitoring, including ground support quality control (pull and shotcrete testing), deformation and seismic monitoring, and routine underground inspections and mapping

Investigate ground-related incidents and falls of ground, leading root cause analysis and continuous improvement in ground control practice

Provide geotechnical input to technical studies, mine planning and life-of-mine design, including surface infrastructure, portals, ventilation raises and dewatering excavations

Manage geotechnical consultants, ground support contractors and the geotechnical budget, including scope, quality and invoice review

Train and coach mining, development and supervisory crews in ground awareness, scaling and ground support installation, and ensure compliance with the Victorian OHS (Mines) Regulations and Earth Resources obligations, including reporting to management and the regulator

Who You Are

You're an experienced underground geotechnical engineer ready to lead. You care about keeping people and workings safe from ground-related hazards and you turn technical analysis into practical standards that crews will follow. You communicate clearly with mining, development and projects teams, you influence operational crews and you enjoy building a function in a growing operation.

Your Background

Tertiary degree in Geotechnical, Mining or Civil Engineering, or Engineering Geology; a postgraduate qualification in geomechanics is highly regarded

At least eight years' geotechnical experience in underground hard rock mining

Strong working knowledge of rock mass characterisation, ground support design, stope and pillar design, and mine-induced seismicity

Proven experience writing and implementing a Ground Control Management Plan and TARPs on an operating mine

Proficiency with geotechnical software such as Rocscience (RS2, Unwedge, Dips), Map3D, FLAC or similar, and with Deswik or equivalent mine design packages

Demonstrated experience managing consultants and contractors, including scope, quality and invoice control, and managing a budget

Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to influence operational crews and build a team in a growing operation

Desirable: experience in a senior or lead site role, Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) or RPEQ status, and experience with narrow-vein or steeply dipping orebodies

The Practical Details

Location: Sunday Creek, VIC (residential)

Roster: 5:2

Contract: Full-time, Permanent

Reports to: Underground Development Manager

Required checks

- Relevant medical and background checks

- Valid driver’s licence

- Right to work & qualifications verification

Ready to Lead Ground Control at Sunday Creek?

If you're ready to lead geotechnical engineering at Sunday Creek we'd love to hear from you. Apply now to join the SXGC team.

About Southern Cross Gold Consolidated Ltd

Southern Cross Gold Consolidated Ltd (SXGC) is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX) and has CHESS Depositary Interests (CDIs) listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX).

We explore for gold and antimony in the Victorian Goldfields. Our 100% owned flagship project at Sunday Creek is the best new grassroots discovery in Australia with a globally leading high-grade hit rate for this stage of the project’s development.

Our results demonstrate high-grades and wide zones of gold and antimony over a 12km mineralised trend. As at 10th June, 2026, we have delivered 88 intersections exceeding 100 g/t Au from just 124km of drilling at Sunday Creek including results such as 1.0 m @ 2,318 g/t Au drilled within 455.3 m @ 7.2 g/t Au and 13.1 m @ 91.7 g/t Au within 331.5 m @ 6.8 g/t Au.

Our corporate objectives are to discover and develop large, long-life, sustainable assets which create value for shareholders and all stakeholders in the community.

Anglo American Australia

Grosvenor Mine an underground steelmaking coal mine produced its first longwall coal in May 2016 and is located in Moranbah, about 190 km south-west of Mackay.

- Provide strategic advice to the Technical Services and Mining Operations departments on how to maximise the value of the operation.

- Advise management and operational staff on geotechnical issues.

- Manage the Strata Defect System and ensure compliance with the Geotechnical Operational Management System.

- Advise and assist engineers with recommendations on geotechnical and hydro-geological issues regarding mine design, planning and operations.

- Understand and comply with all legislative and company safety, health, environment, cost and production objectives, guidelines, procedures, and requirements relevant to the professional management of ground conditions.

- Provide mentoring and training to personnel with respect to strata support systems.

- Tertiary degree in Geotechnical Engineering or similar discipline

- Proven underground coal experience within a Geotechnical Engineering role

- Experience with computer aided mine design programs, geotechnical software, and other business software

- Registered Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ) would be highly advantageous or willingness to obtain recognition

- Ability to understand functionality of business systems and provide relevant data for business purposes

Additional Information

- Attractive roster on offer

- Competitive Salary + 12% Super + Annual Bonus

Evolution Mining is a premier global gold company operating six mines across Australia and Canada. We’re transforming mines and uplifting careers. We took our Cowal Gold Operations underground in just seven years. We’ve extended the mine life of our Ernest Henry Operations to 2040 and doubled its ore reserves. We’re transforming our Red Lake Operations, restoring it as a premier Canadian gold mine. That kind of ambition creates careers, not just jobs. When we asked our people what they enjoy most about working at Evolution, two things came up across every site: career growth and the quality of the people. Here's your opportunity to help shape the future of Northparkes next open pit development. As the  Senior Geotechnical Engineer – Open Pit , you will provide geotechnical leadership for the development of the E28NE open pit, influencing key design, risk management and operational decisions from project establishment through to production. As the Senior Geotechnical Engineer, you'll play a pivotal role in establishing and supporting a major greenfield mining project. Working closely with mining, geology and project stakeholders, you will provide geotechnical expertise that directly influences pit design, slope performance, operational safety and long-term asset value. Working a family friendly 5:2/4:3 roster with 9 hour days, you'll enjoy a great lifestyle balance while contributing to a project that will have a lasting impact on Northparkes future. With multiple open pit developments planned across the operation, this role provides a unique opportunity to influence Northparkes long-term open pit strategy and contribute to future growth projects beyond E28NE. Reporting to the Mining Superintendent – Open Pit, you'll: - Provide technical leadership and assurance for slope stability, ground control and pit wall performance throughout the mine life. - Influence the safe design, development and performance of a new open pit mining operation. - Deliver geotechnical monitoring, analysis and recommendations that support safe operational decision-making. - Develop and enhance geotechnical systems, hazard controls and TARPs that improve site-wide risk management. - Partner with mining, geology, survey and contractor teams to achieve successful project outcomes. - Contribute to the establishment of a high-performing technical team and future Northparkes growth projects. With our E28NE Open Cut Project underway, we’re entering an exciting phase of growth that will underpin an extended mine life underground. This is your opportunity to be part of a career defining project, build new capabilities and contribute to one of Australia’s most exciting operations with underground block cave and sub level cave mines and a number of future open pit operations. At Northparkes, you don’t have to choose between a great career and a great lifestyle; you’ll get both. With flexible work options, opportunities to grow and a team that cares, this is where your bright future starts.

- Recognition program

- Study assistance

- Gym visits

- BP fuel card

- Attractive rosters

- Flexible work options – we know flexibility looks different for everyone

Does this sound like you?

- Bachelor of Engineering (Mining) or equivalent qualification

- Experience in open pit geotechnical engineering, slope stability or mine geotechnical management

- Practical knowledge of geotechnical monitoring, hazard management and risk assessment

- Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills

jobs.title: Environmental Consultant
jobs.summary: Environmental Consultant – Environment and Planning
jobs.description:
Environmental Consultant – Environment and Planning  

At Aurecon, we are engineering optimists who see the world differently. We ask what’s possible and turn ideas into impact. Here, you’ll bring your expertise to challenges that matter, alongside people who think boldly and are determined to make a difference. 

What you’ll do  

As an Environmental Consultant in our Environment and Planning team based in Queensland, you’ll take on environmental and planning approvals, environmental management and environmental design management for major projects, helping shape solutions for our clients and communities. You’ll work across disciplines, test ideas and find better ways to solve complex engineering problems . 

Manage and support environmental and planning approvals for major projects under the guidance of senior staff, developing approvals strategies and resolving issues as projects evolve.  
 Prepare approval applications, environmental and impact assessments, policy advice and technical reports, coordinating and consolidating specialist inputs.  
 Develop environmental management plans and risk assessments, and support construction and operational environmental risk management using standard technical practices, procedures and policies.  
 Interpret Commonwealth and State legislation, policy and approval requirements to advise clients, support stakeholder consultation and liaise with regulators.  
 Contribute across renewable energy, transmission, coal seam gas (CSG), mining, resources, transport, water and other infrastructure projects.  
 Support environmental design management by integrating environmental requirements into project design and delivery with multidisciplinary teams.  
 Assist with project scope, budget, scheduling and resource coordination to deliver quality outcomes on time and within budget.  
 Support proposals, tender submissions and business development opportunities when required.  

You may also be required to undertake other reasonable duties from time to time to support the purpose of the role. 

Your experience and expertise  

A bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental management, environmental policy, planning, engineering, law, or a related discipline. 
 Approximately three to six years of relevant post-graduation experience in environmental planning, approvals, impact assessment or environmental management.  
 Experience in environmental engineering, environmental science, construction, contracting, government or a client-side environment role. Consulting experience is advantageous but not essential.  
 Experience with Commonwealth and State approvals processes, knowledge of environmental policy and legislation, and strong technical analysis skills. Construction environmental management experience is also valued.  
 Project exposure in one or more of the sectors outlined above. Experience across multiple sectors is advantageous but not essential.  
 Strong report writing, verbal communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to provide well-reasoned advice, manage multiple tasks and work autonomously or collaboratively with technical teams. 

How we support your growth  

Engineering possibilities for your career means having room to shape what comes next. You bring your ambition and commitment to lifelong learning, and we provide the foundation and development to help you turn your aspirations into achievement. 

The Aurecon Way guides how we think, act and work together, what we value and how we invest in our people. You’ll be part of a culture built on clear expectations, optimism and determination, where you can feel safe, included and empowered to speak openly, think boldly and deliver brilliantly. 

Who we are  

We are an engineering consultancy with more than 6,000 people across Australia, New Zealand and Asia. We believe the world needs people who can engineer possibilities; people who can create infrastructure that makes life better for people and the planet. That is why we are here – to bring ideas to life, the Aurecon way. 

Ready to explore what’s possible?  

If this sounds like your next step, we’d love to hear from you. We value diverse experiences and welcome applications for part-time or flexible working arrangements. For recruitment adjustments, contact WorkplaceAdjustment@aurecongroup.com.  

Our hiring decisions are made by people, not AI. We’re most interested in your thinking and experience, so please ensure your application reflects your authentic perspective.

jobs.description:
Civil/Structural Engineer – Inspections & Repair Design

Are you ready to elevate your career while enjoying real flexibility and significant earning potential? Buildfix is on a mission to reinvent structural repair, and we're seeking an ambitious Civil/Structural Engineer to join our expansion in Melbourne.

If you're looking for autonomy, uncapped earning potential and a rewarding career solving real structural challenges, this could be your next move.

Why Join Buildfix?

Work–Life Balance – Flexible working hours to help you balance your personal life and professional success.

Exceptional Earning Potential – Receive a regular weekly base plus an uncapped share of the revenue from the jobs you win and manage. Your technical expertise, customer relationships and ability to deliver results contribute directly to your earning potential.

Innovative Repair Solutions – Work with specialist products, repair methods and technology developed within Buildfix, helping customers resolve challenging building problems.

Growth & Development – Comprehensive training in our products, repair techniques and systems, including interstate opportunities for specialised training.

Advanced Mobile Software – Our own AI-assisted software brings inspection scheduling, repair detailing and client management together, reducing administration and unnecessary office time.

Your Work Essentials Covered – Company car, fuel card, iPad with company apps, inspection equipment and phone provided.

About the Role

Structural Assessments – Inspect mainly residential properties, diagnose structural issues and develop practical, cost-effective, non-invasive repair solutions for everyday Melburnians.

Build Trust & Manage Customer Relationships – Explain suitable repair methods, their benefits, limitations and costs. Build trust, follow up proposals and turn leads into confirmed work, with the satisfaction of helping customers who value your expertise and appreciate your effort.

Autonomy & Job Satisfaction – Enjoy the freedom to manage your day and tackle structural problems others struggle to solve. Work alongside Buildfix's own trades and technicians to see your solutions put into practice, taking pride in the results and the difference you make for customers.

Become a Key Member of the Team – Join a close-knit team of experienced engineers who share knowledge, support each other and grow together. Your ideas and expertise will help shape our team as we work towards a common goal: changing the way structural repairs are done. You'll help us lead the way.

You'll work under the guidance and support of Chris Brown, our National Engineering Manager, who is a structural engineer based in Sydney. Your work will take you across Melbourne, with travel to surrounding areas during busy periods and occasional interstate travel.

What We're Looking For

A degree in Civil or Structural Engineering, membership of Engineers Australia and proven structural inspection experience.

Strong practical knowledge of building construction, structural movement and defects.

The confidence to explain technical issues simply, design suitable repair solutions and win the customer's trust.

A highly driven, self-motivated individual who takes initiative, follows through and enjoys solving problems, providing real help for customers.

Strong communication and the ability to manage customers, trades and technicians professionally.

A high-performing individual who understands that greater rewards come from consistent effort, strong results and delivering real value to customers.

Enthusiasm for learning specialist repair methods and contributing to a business that challenges conventional thinking.

A current Australian driver's licence and willingness to travel for assessments and training.

At Buildfix, we reward commitment, skill and outstanding performance. You'll join a close team with the opportunity to grow your expertise, increase your earnings and see your recommendations become completed repairs.

Ready for your next challenge?

If you're ready to take the next step in your career with a company that values your effort, offers work you can take pride in and rewards the results you deliver, we'd like to meet you.

As a Lead Senior Civil & Structural Engineer, you will bring strong technical judgement, commercial awareness and a relationship-led approach to consulting. If you are ready to bring your technical leadership, customer focus and commercial mindset to a global team solving some of the world’s most complex challenges, we’d like to hear from you. Apply now and be part of the Worley journey.

Who We Are

Worley is a global professional services company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia. Right now, we’re bridging two worlds as we accelerate to more sustainable energy sources while helping our customers provide the energy, chemicals and resources that society needs now.

We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value over the life of their portfolio of assets. We solve complex problems by finding integrated, data-centric solutions from the first stages of engineering and consulting through to installation and commissioning.

Join us and help drive innovation and sustainability in our projects.

What You’ll Do

- Lead civil and structural engineering delivery for regional industrial, resources and energy customers.

- Deliver discipline-specific engineering services that satisfy Worley and its clients and meet applicable statutory and regulatory requirements on time and within budget as part of the delivery team.

- Build trusted customer relationships and understand the operational, commercial and technical drivers behind their projects.

- Identify opportunities, shape scopes and support proposals, estimates and work-winning strategies.

- Provide technical assurance across calculations, design reports, drawings, specifications, reviews and site queries.

- Mentor engineers and designers, supporting strong delivery, collaboration and capability development across local and remote teams.

- Represent Worley in client meetings, site engagements, technical discussions and regional business development activities.

What You’ll Bring

- Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering or a recognised related discipline.

- Extensive civil and structural engineering experience, ideally within mining, energy, chemicals, hydrocarbons, ports, process plant, infrastructure or heavy industry.

- Strong brownfield, operating asset and site-based engineering experience.

- Highly effective technical and practical engineering skills, with the ability to consistently deliver quality, accurate and timely work for Worley and its customers.

- Strong client-facing and business development capability, with the ability to cultivate trusted relationships, identify opportunities, prepare proposals and secure repeat work while maintaining excellence in technical delivery.

- Practical knowledge of steel, concrete, foundations, drainage, pavements, access systems, equipment supports and constructability.

- Experience with structural analysis and 3D modelling/drafting packages, and an understanding of structural drafting workflows.

- Demonstrated experience with Space Gass structural analysis software.

- Experience using finite element analysis (FEA) software such as Strand7.

- Experience working with and managing diverse teams across multiple geographic locations.

- Chartered Professional Engineer status, registration on an appropriate national engineering register, and any relevant state-based professional engineering registration such as RPEQ or RPEV, or eligibility to obtain these registrations.

Why you should apply

- Work locally on nationally significant industrial assets and projects.

- Combine technical delivery, client leadership and business growth in one influential role.

- Join a supportive multidisciplinary team with access to broader global expertise.

- Develop your career through varied work, mentoring and direct exposure to clients and operating facilities.

- Enjoy a regional lifestyle without stepping away from complex engineering challenges.

- Build trusted relationships and see your engineering solutions progress into construction and operation.

Moving forward together

Whatever your ambition, there’s a path for you here. And there’s no barrier to your potential career success. We’ll help you take control of your growth and learning journey to gain the skills you need right now and for the future.

You’ll have the freedom to choose how you work and which opportunities you explore. We’ll encourage you to achieve your goals and give you the space to thrive personally and professionally.

Join us to broaden your horizons, explore diverse opportunities and be part of delivering sustainable change.

If you are a technically strong engineer who enjoys being close to clients, turning ideas into delivered outcomes and helping grow a regional business, we would like to hear from you.

jobs.summary: Structural Engineer / Inspections – Melbourne's Eastern Suburbs
jobs.description:
Structural Engineer / Inspections – Melbourne's Eastern Suburbs

Full time | Weekly base pay + a share of the jobs you win and manage

You understand buildings. You enjoy working out why something has moved, what caused the damage and how it can be repaired. You also enjoy helping the homeowner understand it.

At Buildfix, those skills are at the centre of your role—and directly contribute to your earnings.

We're looking for an experienced structural engineer who sees solutions where others see problems. Someone motivated, practical and comfortable taking responsibility, who wants to be part of a close team building a better way to repair Australian homes.

After five years of growth across Melbourne's northern and western suburbs, we're expanding our permanent presence in the eastern suburbs. This is an opportunity to help shape that next stage.

Share in the work you win and manage. Receive a regular weekly base plus a share of the revenue from your jobs. Your engineering judgement, ability to explain the solution and care for the customer all contribute to your results.

Company car, fuel card, inspection equipment and phone provided. You'll be equipped for your work on the road, with work travel and communication costs covered.

Enjoy life outside work. A role built around field assessments, mobile technology and effective task management, with flexibility and home at a normal time most days.

Solve problems that matter. Help everyday homeowners understand what is happening to their home and find practical repair solutions that can reduce disruption, protect their property and give them confidence in the way forward.

Work independently, with people behind you. Take ownership of your day while being part of a close team of structural engineers who share knowledge, discuss difficult cases and support each other. You'll report to our National Engineering Manager.

Learn specialist methods. Receive comprehensive training in Buildfix's products, repair techniques and systems.

Spend more time using your expertise. Our own AI-assisted mobile software brings assessments, repair detailing, quoting and task management together, reducing routine administration and unnecessary office time.

About the role

You'll meet homeowners who are often concerned about cracking, movement or uneven floors. They need someone who can listen, investigate and explain what their home needs.

Your ability to educate the customer is just as important as your ability to identify the problem. You'll explain the cause, talk through suitable repair options and help them understand the benefits, limitations and costs.

You'll take responsibility for:

Conducting residential structural inspections and diagnosing the causes of damage.

Developing practical, cost-effective repair scopes using Buildfix's products and methods.

Preparing clear repair details and quotes.

Answering questions, following up recommendations and helping homeowners make informed decisions about proceeding.

Managing the jobs you win, maintaining customer relationships and coordinating with our repair teams.

Keeping your assessments, records and tasks accurate and up to date.

Your main service area will be Melbourne's eastern suburbs, with travel across greater Melbourne and surrounding areas during busy periods. Occasional interstate travel may also be required, including for specialised training.

This is a field role with plenty of driving, customer contact and independent work.

Who will suit this role?

You'll bring:

A degree in Civil or Structural Engineering, with the relevant registration to practise in Victoria.

At least five years' experience covering structural inspections and residential construction design.

Strong practical knowledge of residential buildings, structural movement and defects.

The ability to explain technical issues simply, listen carefully and handle challenging customer questions.

Motivation, initiative and the discipline to manage your own workload.

Pride in finding a suitable solution and following through to see it delivered.

A current Australian driver's licence and willingness to travel throughout the service area.

Build something lasting with Buildfix

Established in Sydney more than 13 years ago, Buildfix has grown into a national structural repair business with engineering at its centre. We manufacture our own products, develop our own repair solutions and bring assessment and delivery together within one business.

Our reputation rests on the quality of our work and how we look after homeowners. We have team members who have been with us for more than a decade, and we're building for the long term—with opportunities for our people as the business continues to grow.

This role won't suit everyone.

It goes beyond inspecting a property and explaining what's wrong. Your role is to show homeowners what we can do for them, explain a suitable solution and give them the confidence to move forward.

You'll own the customer relationship and the job from the first assessment through to completion. That means being accountable for your advice, repair scope, communication, follow-through and how the job is managed.

You'll have an experienced team behind you, but you'll be expected to lead from the front through both the satisfying wins and the difficult days. We're looking for someone with a winning instinct: motivated to find solutions, earn the customer's trust, handle setbacks and see things through.

The independence and financial rewards come with real responsibility. If you take pride in owning an outcome and delivering what you've promised, you'll find plenty of opportunity here.

Interested? Your application starts with a conversation.

We're GHD.

We don't do hair. But we do straighten out some of the world's biggest challenges.

Since 1928, we've been wholly owned by our employees. Today, we are 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals working in over 160 offices across five continents — Asia, Australia, Europe, North and South America, and the Pacific region.

Who could you be at GHD?

In Newcastle, our DDO - Architecture & Structures team is looking for our next Graduate Structural Engineer!

This role offers the opportunity to build experience across a range of structural engineering activities, providing a strong foundation for your career while developing your technical, analytical and engineering capabilities.

Our two-year Graduate Development Program is designed to give you a smooth start to your consulting career. Alongside your peers, managers and mentors, we'll help you detangle any challenges along the way. You'll work collaboratively with peers across other disciplines within GHD, as well as with our clients, and connect across the business to share insights, knowledge and improve your overall technical capabilities.

A frizz-free application process:

We want your journey to be as smooth as possible, so here's everything you need to help you prep like a pro:

- Your CV: This gives us a snapshot of what you've studied and your experiences, both paid and unpaid.
- A cover letter: Think of this as your chance to show us where you'd love to grow within GHD, while letting your communication skills shine.
- Your transcript: This helps us understand what you've been learning, from your core subjects to the electives that sparked your curiosity.

Your journey to joining GHD:

Here's what to expect, step by step:

- Virtual Assessments: If you make it through the first stage, you'll record some answers to a few straightforward questions and complete some cognitive games. This helps us get a better sense of your work style and alignment to GHD Graduate roles.
- Meet the team: If you're successful, you'll have a face-to-face interview (wherever possible) with your prospective team. We'll chat through some behavioural based questions to learn more about your skills and experience. It's also a chance for you to get to know us!
- Offer: Congratulations! We'll talk through all the finer details, like salary, your start date, our onboarding process and what to expect before your first day.

We're committed to being as inclusive as possible and giving everyone an equitable chance of getting through our application process. If you identify as someone who is neurodiverse or have a disability and need adjustments to any part of the process, let us know in your application form—we're here to help.

Start dates and opportunities

Most of our full-time roles kick off in February 2027, though some teams might have earlier start dates in mid-2026. Plus, there might also be casual work opportunities throughout your final year of study to give you a head start.

Ready to shine?

If you've got your documents polished and prepped, the application should only take 10-15 minutes.

GHD: The Power of Commitment

At GHD, we don't just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day. Community impact is important to us, influencing how we work, our projects and how we give back. Our GHD in the Community program partners with not-for-profit organisations so that we can work on pro-bono projects, as well as volunteering and fundraising for philanthropic and humanitarian causes. As a business, we also channel some of our profits into the GHD Foundation, a registered charity that addresses disadvantage and inequality in children accessing STEAM education in the countries where we live and work.

Within GHD, our employee groups and networks help us foster community, find our tribe, and celebrate what makes us unique. These groups play a big part in our global diversity, equity and inclusion strategy, creating spaces for meaningful and safe conversations, connecting with likeminded individuals, and creating a voice to leadership.

jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The Global Engineering Strategy team (GES) is looking for a results-oriented, inventive senior geotechnical engineer to drive front end geotechnical engineering for new owned and leased site developments.

You will lead the geotechnical engineering due diligence and design ready geotechnical efforts for new and expanding regions, while maintaining the highest performance standards and utilizing innovation to reduce budgets and increase efficiency.

You will sit within the Design Engineering team of the broader Data Center Engineering (DCE) organization. You will work with our Real Estate, Risk and Resiliency, Environmental, Pre-Construction and related partner teams on global design strategy implementation.

You will assist in data center site selection, review of due diligence reports, lead geotechnical investigations and preliminary engineering and play a pivotal role in the delivery of data center designs.

- Are strong leaders who can prioritize well, communicate clearly, and have a consistent track record of delivery.

- Provide creative engineering balanced with high quality and customer focus.

- Work as part of a team to accomplish our goals.

- Perform technical design engineering diligence for global regions.

- Thrive in a fast-paced environment.

- Lead project teams through ambiguity.

- Understand the best practices for data center project delivery.

- Have extensive experience within the arena of domestic and international data center delivery.

The Senior Geotechnical Engineer responsibilities include:

- Collaborating with internal stakeholders during the due diligence and pre-design phases to oversee the process and ensure design requirements are considered.

- Collaborating with internal teams to gather data to ensure pre-requisites for start of design stage are met.

- Leading due diligence and pre-design geotechnical investigations, managing internal partners and your external vendor consultants, ensuring design ready geotechnical deliverables are completed and handed over for successful design execution.

- Rollout strategy of new data center design types and intercepts that impact geotechnical investigations and engineering.

- Provide engineering design decisions to the partner teams for strategic planning and region selection.

- Collaborate with other DCE teams developing new data center infrastructure products, and design execution team disciplines such as civil engineering, structural engineering and architects to assess how our various design types, BOD and products can be deployed for a certain site development project.

- Ability to work on concurrent projects in multiple geographical regions.

- Escalate issues as required and communicate clearly and effectively at the appropriate level of detail with people from a wide range of technical abilities, backgrounds and levels of leadership.

Travel will occasionally be necessary but shouldn't be more than 25%.

Senior Geotechnical Engineer (Strong Senior / Associate Principal pathway)

- Location: Brisbane, QLD (4 days in office)

- Employment type: Full-time, permanent

- Reports to: Principal Geotechnical Engineer

About Client

Our Client is a Brisbane-based engineering consultancy delivering specialist geotechnical, civil and structural engineering services across infrastructure, transport and resources projects, with a particularly strong footprint in Queensland and Southeast Queensland. We pride ourselves on a high-performance, values-driven culture where engineers take genuine ownership of their work and are trusted to deliver.

About the Role

Our Client is looking for a Strong Senior Geotechnical Engineer to join our Brisbane team as 2IC to their Principal Geotechnical Engineer, with a clear pathway into a Principal role within 1-2 years. This is a hands-on, technically demanding position that combines detailed design leadership, mentoring of a developing team, and active site involvement. It has been deliberately scoped to attract someone who is ready to step up, not a typical Senior, but an engineer with the depth, judgement and presence to operate at Associate Principal level.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 12 months, you will independently lead the geotechnical design on multiple concurrent projects, mentor 3-4 graduate to mid-level engineers, deliver IFC-quality reports and drawings with minimal rework, build credibility with clients and contractors on site, and be on track to take on Principal-level responsibilities.

Non-Negotiable Requirements

- IEAust Chartered (CPEng) and/or RPEQ qualified.

- Approximately 15 years geotechnical engineering experience, with a track record of leading detailed design on infrastructure projects.

- Strong design capability across the full geotechnical spectrum: shallow and pile foundations (including bridge piles using Pell's, Rowe & Armitage, Broms Method, soil springs and pile settlement), pile group analysis (Piglet, or demonstrable equivalent), earth retaining structures (gravity, cantilever, RC L-shape, anchored, MSE), slope stability (Slope/W), soil and rock slope stabilisation, ground anchors, micro-piles, ground improvement of soft soils (surcharge, wick drains, geosynthetic reinforcement, CMC), and temporary works design.

- Slope Risk Assessment to RMS Version 4 - this is a hard requirement with no equivalent accepted.

- Demonstrated ability to work independently with minimal supervision and full accountability for outcomes.

- Construction experience associated with the technical capabilities above, and willingness to undertake site rotations of 1-3 weeks.

- Eligible to work in Australia (international candidates with the right technical fit will be considered, with sponsorship available).

Highly Regarded (developing skills welcomed)

- Instrumentation and monitoring interpretation.

- Advanced experience preparing IFC drawing packages and specification documentation.

- Prior experience acting as a 2IC or stepping toward a Principal-level role.

Who You Are

- You take initiative and resolve issues rather than wait for direction.

- You are comfortable making the call when information is incomplete and confident in defending your reasoning.

- You communicate engineering concepts clearly to less experienced colleagues, plan and organise work effectively, and follow through to ensure delivery quality.

- You are flexible, commercially aware, and willing to go beyond the minimum to land a successful project outcome.

What The Client Offers

- Base salary $200 - $210K + super

- A clear, supported pathway to Principal Geotechnical Engineer within 1-2 years.

- Direct mentorship from our Principal Engineer and a culture that genuinely invests in technical development.

- Diverse, technically interesting project work across QLD infrastructure.

- Sponsorship available for the right international candidate.

jobs.description:
At KCB, we pride ourselves on our global reputation for technical excellence and our innovative approach to solving complex problems. Our diverse and inclusive teams bring creative perspectives, and our size allows us to tackle exciting projects in a positive work environment. Our tagline, "Down to Earth / Up to the Challenge," says a lot about who we are.

Our projects include tailings and waste storage facilities, water management structures, water dams, and mine infrastructure projects. We are engaged in the entire project cycle from green field studies, feasibility, site investigation, design, construction, commissioning, operations and maintenance, and closure. This allows our professionals to challenge themselves while gaining valuable engineering and project management experience on fascinating projects.

We are looking for a Senior Tailings Engineer to join our Brisbane-based engineering team to work on mining and resource projects located in Australia and overseas. Your experience will be applied to the planning, investigation, assessment, design and construction of tailings and water dams and waste storage for our existing mining and non-resource clients. Career development can be managed to support personal preferences such as niche, technical design specialists, or project participation in both technical dam engineering scopes and project management, or all-round dam engineering specialists, such as the responsible persons or Engineers of Record.

If you are registered, or eligible to register as a Professional Engineer, have a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Civil or Geotechnical Engineering and a minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in the mining or related industries, we want to hear from you!

This senior role will give you the opportunity to:

- work with our global team which includes many world-recognised tailings engineers

- fill a technical role focused on tailings management design with conventional or alternative technologies, dam design, mining geo-structures and operations support

- deliver projects successfully and be accountable for project planning, control, and direction

- prepare and review technical reports, drawings, specifications, risk assessments, bill of quantities, and cost estimates

- sustain client relationships and develop new business

- join a dynamic company of motivated and hardworking professionals committed to delivering high quality engineering, geoscience, and environmental services

- travel to project sites across Australia and worldwide

We value your:

- Strong initiative, innovation, and commitment to technical excellence as well as your enthusiasm and drive toward long-term success.

- Enthusiasm to learn and increase your technical skills and professional experience.

- Ability to work autonomously or within a project team with like-minded professionals in offices around Australia and overseas.

- Superior verbal and written communication skills including your experience in writing proposals, technical reports, and general project correspondence.

- Exceptional team spirit, interpersonal skills and your ability to build long-term, successful relationships with our clients and our project teams.

- Ability to develop and grow relationships with a variety of clients.

What we offer in addition to an exciting role:

- Additional Superannuation: 2.5% extra to secure your future.

- Income Protection Insurance: Peace of mind for you and your family.

- Parental and Volunteer Leave: Support for your personal and community commitments.

- Novated Leasing: Flexible vehicle leasing options.

- Hybrid Working Policy: Balance work and life with our flexible approach.

- Social and Mental Well-being Initiatives: Programs to support your overall well-being.

- Training and Development Opportunities: Continuous growth and learning.

- Additional incentives may be available dependent on the performance of the company, business unit and individual.

This role offers a dynamic and collaborative work environment, with opportunities for professional growth and development.

About Us:

KCB Australia Pty Ltd (KCB) is a multi-disciplinary consulting firm providing engineering, geoscience and environmental services globally. We offer a full range of services from our offices in Australia, Canada, USA, UK, Brazil and Peru. Read more about us here

We respect the uniqueness that makes you, you. We are committed to employment equity and encourage applications from all qualified career seekers. KCB is an Australian Business Awards Employer of Choice recipient (2015-2024).

jobs.description:
Beca HunterH2O Beca HunterH2O is the Australian water business of one of Asia Pacific's largest independent advisory, design and engineering consultancies, Beca. We are a formidable team of 300+ water specialists, passionate about healthy and sustainable communities wherever we work. Using our deep knowledge and broader capability, we collaborate with our clients through city and regional offices operating in Sydney, Melbourne, Newcastle, Tamworth, Brisbane, Adelaide and Fiji. Combining the capability of our expert water specialists with access to more than 4000 multi-disciplinary specialists we can bring the best of Beca to our clients. With our purpose – to make everyday better, and our four values – partnership, tenacity, enjoyment and care – sitting at the heart of everything we do, we can truly realise our vision of 'Creative people together transforming our world'.

The Opportunity

While water is the world's most precious resource, at Beca HunterH2O, our people are our most precious resource. We are passionate about what we do and the culture we have developed. The more diverse we are, the better our ideas, strategies and client solutions will be. As our pipeline of work grows, we are seeking a Senior Structural Engineer to join our multidisciplinary water team in Newcastle.

Ideally, you will have experience in the structural design of water and wastewater treatment plants, reservoirs, pump stations and conveyance pipelines, with previous tasks including the review of design requirements, site investigations, calculations, modelling, oversight of drafting and the preparation of reports and specifications. Building strong client relationships and demonstrating your ability to understand our client's core business you will be able to provide solutions and service to clients both off and on site.

Stepping into a supportive and inclusive work environment that values diversity and continuous improvement you will be given opportunities for professional growth and development as well as mentorship from experienced engineers.

About You

You will be seeking fulfilment in autonomy, career flexibility and working for a business that can provide purpose and relevance in what you do. With outstanding communication skills and the ability to influence and drive successful project outcomes for the business and our valuable clients you will have gained experience working in a consulting environment delivering projects as part of a multi‐disciplinary and multi‐office project team.

Your ideal skills and expertise:

- Bachelor's degree in civil (structural) engineering

- A minimum of 8 years' experience in water and wastewater treatment and conveyance (pipeline) design

- Experience in managing packages on small to medium engineering design projects

- Provision of specialist knowledge, technical review and advice and technical leadership in your area of expertise

- Knowledge of safety in design, constructability and operational practices and relevant Australian standards and WSAA codes

- Knowledge of risk management with the ability to identify project and design related risks

- A commitment to working safely, and within the company's HSEQ systems

- Strong problem‐solving skills with the ability to collaborate across a multidisciplinary team

- Well‐developed written and verbal communication skills to interact with clients and a broad range of audiences

- Coaching and mentoring of team members

- Ability to travel on occasions as the work requires

What We Offer

A career with Beca will provide you with:

- Flexibility & Wellbeing: We recognise that achieving a work‐life balance is unique to everyone. Enjoy flexible working options to manage your personal and family priorities, along with dedicated leave for wellbeing and community engagement.

- Belonging & Ownership: Join a diverse and inclusive team where collaboration and creativity thrive. Bring your whole self to work and take advantage of unique shareholder opportunities to share in our collective success.

- Parental Leave: Take time for what matters most with up to 14 weeks of fully paid parental leave, inclusive of all genders.

- Career Growth & Development: Your growth is our priority! Benefit from continuous learning through our training programs and support for professional accreditation, including pathways to Chartership with Engineers Australia. Work alongside industry leaders and gain hands‐on experience to empower your career potential.

Beca prides itself on supporting a diverse and inclusive culture – open to inputs from creative people of all genders, ethnicity, identity, thought and experiences.

Who is Beca?

Beca is one of the Asia‐Pacific region's largest employee‐owned professional services consultancies. Our team of over 4000 professionals is diverse enough to bring a wide range of perspectives and expertise to every client and challenge, creating resourceful, smart solutions from our collective experience and insights. 'Creative people together transforming our world' is our vision. It reflects our culture, our aspirations and our purpose – to make everyday better.

At Beca we make everyday better for our clients, our people and our community and your involvement makes it possible.

Our size and agility mean you're not just on the fringes; you're making a visible difference, partnering to develop and deliver solutions from the ground up. As a people‐focused business, we understand that work‐life balance means a lot of different things to different people and that it's not always easy juggling work with everything else life throws at us. This is why we are happy to discuss flexible working arrangements for all opportunities in the Beca team.

Balfour Beatty is a leading national infrastructure and construction company with more than a century of heritage in Scotland, delivering key projects that strengthen communities and improve national connectivity. jobs.description:
We're a bold team with a bright future; and we're looking for people who want to be part of it.

Evolution Mining is a premier global gold company operating six mines across Australia and Canada. We're transforming mines and uplifting careers. We took our Cowal Gold Operations underground in just seven years. We've extended the mine life of our Ernest Henry Operations to 2040 and doubled its ore reserves. We'retransforming our Red Lake Operations, restoring it as a premier Canadiangoldmine. That kind of ambition creates careers, not just jobs.

When we asked our people what they enjoy most about working at Evolution, two things came up across every site: career growth and the quality of the people. Here, you'll work alongside people who care, who push one another to be better, with leaders who arethere to support you.

What's the opportunity?

This is an opportunity to play a critical role in the success of one of Australia's most significant open pit and underground mining operations. As our Geotechnical Engineer (Underground and Open Pit), you'll help shape safe, productive and sustainable mining activities through geotechnical expertise, technical analysis and collaborative problem solving.

Working an attractive 8:6 roster with 12 hour day shifts at our Cowal Gold Operations near West Wyalong, you'll enjoy extended time at home while contributing to the continued growth of our expanding underground operation. You'll work closely with technical and operational teams, influencing key decisions that directly impact mine safety, stability and production performance.

Reporting to the Senior Geotechnical Engineer, you'll:

- Influence safe and productive mining through geotechnical design and analysis.

- Help manage critical ground control, rockfall and geotechnical risks across the operation.

- Partner with mining engineers and operational teams to optimise ground stability and recovery.

- Build and maintain geotechnical models that support informed decision-making and risk management.

- Provide geotechnical input that supports the successful delivery of development and infrastructure projects.

- Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen safety, reliability and operational performance.

Why Cowal Gold Operations?

At Cowal, our never-say-never attitude has led to mine life extension to 2042 as we have boldly reimagined our future. We took our operations there underground in just seven years. Today, you can work on the surface or underground. With open pit and processing all on one site, the operational diversity is ideal for uplifting careers. Live nearby and enjoy the regional lifestyle and close-knit communities. The future here is bright; you could be part of it.

What we offer you

We support, develop and reward you to ensure you have a bright future. Here's how we back that up:

- Relocation support

- Salary packaging (e.g. novated car leasing, remote area housing)

- Life insurance and income protection

- Quarterly performance bonuses

- Employee share scheme – have a real stake in the company's success

- Attractive parental leave benefits (18 weeks)

- Recognition program

- Study assistance

- Discounted health insurance

- Discounted gym membership

- Attractive rosters

- Bus transportation to and from West Wyalong at the beginning and end of your shift

- Flexible work options – we know flexibility looks different for everyone

Does this sound like you?

- Tertiary qualifications in Mining Engineering, Geoscience, Civil Engineering (Geomechanics) or a related discipline.

- Geotechnical experience within a mining environment.

- Knowledge of geotechnical controls, mining operations and risk management principles.

- Experience with geotechnical modelling and CAD software.

- Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills.

- A proactive approach to safety and continuous improvement.

Experience in underground hard rock mining and ground control management will be highly regarded.

Ready to create your career highlight with us?

As our name suggests, change and evolution are in our DNA. If you'd like to work with a team that turns challenges into opportunities and delivers on its bold ambitions, we want to hear from you.

Find out more about us at our Careers site.

Overview Geosyntec Mining (formerly Red Earth Engineering) is a specialist engineering consultancy and recognised technical leader in mine waste, tailings, geotechnical engineering and geosynthetic containment. Our mission is to help clients succeed by delivering exceptional service and innovative best-value solutions for their emerging issues related to energy, the environment, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. We are a consultant of choice for several major mining, resource sector and land development companies with operations in Australia. Our expertise, combined with Geosyntec’s world-class reputation in hydrogeology, geochemistry, geotechnical engineering, seismicity and risk, allows us to assist our clients in meeting their engineering challenges and better understanding their risk. As an example of our commitment to leading the industry in innovation and technical excellence, we have recently announced the establishment of an advanced testing facility led by Dr. David Reid. We have an opportunity available for a  Senior - Tailings / Geotechnical Engineer to join our  Brisbane, Perth, Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide, Gold Coast or Hobart office. This position is well-suited for a talented, experienced individual who is interested in contributing to and managing innovative and challenging projects including several projects where we are current the designated Engineer or Record.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

This role focuses on support our client’s tailings and mine waste management and operational teams to ensure their facilities are safe. Compliance to the latest standards (which are evolving) is critical for mining companies to demonstrate their commitment to ESG and for the Social License to Operate. This role forms part of our team to provide the technical and operation support for Tailings Storage Facilities (TSFs) and Water Storage Facilities (WSF).

As a Senior - Tailings / Geotechnical Engineer, this role requires the application of the tasks listed below (geotechnical engineer), but also an expanding knowledge of all elements and disciplines required to design these facilities, such as hydrogeology, process, geochemistry, water, civil engineering and social engagement.

Some Of The Key Responsibilities May Include

- Civil/Geotechnical/Tailings dam design;

- Geotechnical analyses using various software packages;

- Understanding of tailing deposition modelling (Muk3D)

- Geotechnical and environmental site characterisation;

- Development and management of instrumentation monitoring systems;

- Some Project/task management and proposal preparation support;

- Preparation of engineering reports, design calculations, drawings, technical specifications;

Education and Licensure

- Bachelor's degree in civil or geotechnical engineering or a related field. (required)

- Advanced degree in civil or geotechnical engineering or a related field. (preferred)

- Professional registration (preferred but not essential)

Skills, Experience And Qualifications

- Directly relevant experience in a consulting environment; or equivalent combination of education and experience. (required)

- 5 to 10+ years of consulting experience operating within a geotechnical practice group

- Knowledge of relevant geotechnical engineering software. (required)

- Knowledge of numerical modeling tools. (preferred)

- Ability to succeed in a fast-paced consulting environment, handling multiple project assignments, meeting strict deadlines, and traveling to client facilities as needed. (required)

- Civil or tailings engineering general

- Experience in the GIS, CAD or Tailings Modelling software (i.e. QGIS, 12d, AutoCAD, Civil3D, or Muk3D)

- Familiarity with dam safety guidelines including ANCOLD, GISTM, CDA and WA-DMR

- Excellent writing and communication skills. (required)

- Field work and overnight travel may be required.

- Valid Australian driver’s license and a satisfactory driving record for business travel. (required)

Why are we hiring?

We are seeing significant growth in our projects value and pipeline. We want to be able to meet the needs of repeat clients, and to take on new clients whose projects add value to the community we operate in.

 We’re looking for Project Engineers to join our Complex Civils & Structures team in Auckland , working on some of the region’s most exciting infrastructure projects. 

This is a great role for an experienced engineer who enjoys variety, technical challenge and seeing work move from plan to delivery. You’ll work across reinforced concrete and heavy civil infrastructure projects, helping bridge the gap between design, planning and construction. 

This diverse portfolio, will include work in the following areas:
 Bridges, retaining walls, piling and complex structural works 
 Underpasses and transport structures, level crossings 
 Major infrastructure projects such as Papakura to Drury, Penlink and upcoming water infrastructure projects 
 Wastewater treatment plants, pump stations and complex pipelines 

If you bring strong experience delivering reinforced concrete structures, we’re keen to hear from you. 

Key role responsibilities 
 Manage the teams and sub-contractors within your area and coordinate with other teams to ensure optimisation of resources and efficiency
 Plan the execution of the works and develop construction methodology for all elements of the works
 Provide a monthly forecast of cost to complete to the commercial manager, and an estimate of the work completed in terms of percentages complete to the planner
 Provide technical advice and resolve on-site issues as they arise
 Maintain a safe and tidy site, assisting in the development of management systems and ensuring compliance within your team
 Monitor expenses, process invoices, and contribute to financial reporting.
 Undertake regular inspections to ensure that safety, environmental, and quality standards are achieved across the projects

Good Work equals Good Benefits 
 Company vehicle
 KiwiSaver employer contributions
 Parental leave top-up payment with additional return to work support
 Family scholarships
 Ongoing training and development, career growth and progression opportunities
 Additional Fuel discount card
 Great discounts at a wide range of retailers
 Medical insurance “an eligibility period applies”
 Life insurance 
 At Fulton Hogan, we genuinely care about the wellbeing of our people and giving them the tools and opportunities they need to succeed and grow with us. 

We’re looking for someone with: 
 A Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering at NZQF Level 7+
 Have 5 years’ experience with Structures / Heavy Civil experience
 Have a portfolio that includes strongly in reinforced concrete, bridges or/and treatment plants and pipelines delivery
 Hold proven experience in programming and managing budgets
 Excellent leadership qualities
 Demonstrated excellent interpersonal and communication skills

Ko wai mātou | About us 
 At Fulton Hogan, Good Work is more than what we deliver. It’s how we show up for each other and the communities we work in. We’re a friendly, forward moving team that backs good ideas, values low ego and knows when to have a laugh and when to switch on. 

How to apply 
 If you’re ready to help deliver complex infrastructure that makes a lasting difference, we’d love to hear from you. 

Please tailor your CV to a maximum of three pages . In your cover letter , highlight your experience in reinforced concrete and heavy civil infrastructure, in the areas mentioned above . Focusing on these areas will help us get a clear picture of your technical capability and the value you can bring to the team.

jobs.description:
ACCIONA is a global company, leading in the development of regenerative infrastructure that creates a positive impact on society. Our workforce consists of more than 65,000 professionals, present in more than 40 countries across the five continents, all contributing in our mission to design a better planet. Are you a passionate individual who wants to make a difference, promote sustainable development, and find solutions to the biggest global challenges including climate change, overpopulation, and water scarcity? Come and join us in building the infrastructure our planet needs to achieve a sustainable future. 

Job Description 

Benefits 
 Lead survey on a greenfield rail project from design to build
 Own the link between design models and site delivery
 Grow with ACCIONA leadership pathways and training support

Project Information: 
ACCIONA is part of CoastalTraX, delivering the greenfield works for Stage 1 of The Wave: 19 kilometres of dual-track passenger rail between Beerwah and Caloundra on the Sunshine Coast. Backed by $5.5 billion in joint government funding, the project is part of Queensland’s infrastructure pipeline ahead of Brisbane 2032 and is now in design and preconstruction.

About the Opportunity: 
You will lead the survey function on the greenfield works, reporting to the Construction Manager. As the link between design and site, you will model, review and refine design options with the construction team. Guide your surveying team and subcontractors, run mass haul modelling and spatial analysis, and test site conditions against upcoming program milestones. With the project in design and preconstruction, you can create the data systems and survey practices from the start. You will also keep the wider team across new construction technologies and data capture methods.
 Key accountabilities for the position will be: 
 Lead survey delivery from early planning through to completion
 Model and review design data, including mass haul and spatial analysis
 Oversee construction layout, topographic mapping and boundary retracement
 Guide and mentor surveyors and manage survey subcontractors
 Maintain accurate survey data, as-built records and quality controls
 Manage survey resources, budgets and schedules against program milestones
 Resolve survey discrepancies and work with clients and project stakeholders

Required Skills and Competencies 

What capability and experience will you need to have: 
 Registration as a surveyor
 Diploma in Engineering Surveying or equivalent qualification
 Surveying experience in the civil construction industry
 Advanced 12d or Terramodel skills for modelling and datasets
 Proven ability to lead surveyors and produce method statements

At ACCIONA, we offer a dynamic and challenging work environment where our employees can grow and develop their careers. We provide opportunities for professional development, and our team members are encouraged to bring new ideas and approaches to their work. Our company is dedicated to fostering a culture of inclusiveness and respect where every employee feels valued and supported.

Ready to lead survey on The Wave? Apply now with your current resume.

ACCIONA has been given the Top Employer 2022, 2023, 2024 & 2025 certification in Australia, which certifies the company's commitment to excellence in human resources management and those who focus on putting their people first through their exceptional HR policies. Since establishing a presence in Australia in 2002, ACCIONA has made significant investments in local opportunities and project development. ACCIONA employs more than 3,000 people in its renewable energy, infrastructure and water projects across Australia & New Zealand. 

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and promote equality and diversity. Indigenous Australians and candidates from minority groups are encouraged to apply.
